title: Benjamin Franklin: An American Life
author: Walter Isaacson
text: Published 2004-05-04. Genre: Biography & Memoir. This biography of Benjamin Franklin explores his multifaceted life as a scientist, inventor, diplomat, and political thinker. Walter Isaacson delves into Franklin's personal relationships, including his marriage and estrangement from his son, while also examining the broader context of American and European political history leading up to the Revolutionary War. The book presents Franklin as a pivotal figure in shaping America's national identity. Tone and style: engaging, detailed, narrative-driven. Pacing: methodical, chronologically structured. Themes: identity, politics, innovation, personal relationships. Setting: 18th-century America and Europe. About the author: Walter Seff Isaacson is an American journalist who has written biographies of Henry Kissinger, Benjamin Franklin, Leonardo da Vinci, Albert Einstein, Steve Jobs, Jennifer Doudna, and Elon Musk. As of 2024, Isaacson is a professor at Tulane University and, since 2018, an interviewer for the PBS and CNN news show Amanpour & Company.

title: Why Did the Chicken Cross the World?
author: Andrew Lawler
text: Published 2014. Genre: History. This book explores the history and transformation of the chicken from a wild bird in Southeast Asia to a key source of protein for humanity. It examines the chicken's various roles throughout history, including its significance in medicine, culture, and civilization. The narrative traces the chicken's journey across different regions and its impact on human society. Tone and style: informative, engaging, narrative-driven. Pacing: methodical, exploratory. Themes: domestication, cultural significance, human-animal relationships. Setting: global history of domesticated animals. About the author: Andrew Francis Lawler is an American journalist and author.

title: Siddhartha
author: Herman Hesse
text: Published 1922. Genre: Literary Fiction. Siddhartha follows the journey of a young man named Siddhartha during the time of the Buddha as he seeks spiritual enlightenment. Through various experiences, including asceticism and indulgence, he explores different paths to understanding the nature of existence and self. The novel serves as an allegory for the quest for wisdom and inner peace. Tone and style: lyrical, philosophical, introspective. Pacing: measured, contemplative. Themes: spirituality, self-discovery, enlightenment. Setting: ancient India during the time of the Buddha. About the author: Hermann Karl Hesse was a German-Swiss poet and novelist, and winner of the 1946 Nobel Prize in Literature. His interest in Eastern religious, spiritual, and philosophical traditions, combined with his involvement with Jungian analysis, helped shape his literary work. His best-known novels include Demian, Steppenwolf, Siddhartha, Narcissus and Goldmund, and The Glass Bead Game, each of which explores an individual's search for authenticity, self-knowledge, and spirituality.

title: Americanah
author: Chimamanda Adichie
text: Published 1969. Genre: Literary Fiction. Americanah follows Ifemelu and Obinze, a Nigerian couple whose love is tested by their experiences in America and England. Ifemelu, now a successful blogger in the U.S., grapples with her identity and race, while Obinze faces challenges in London, including deportation. Their eventual reunion in Nigeria forces them to confront how their lives have changed and the impact of their choices on their relationship. Tone and style: thoughtful, engaging, contemporary. Pacing: measured, character-driven. Themes: identity, race, immigration, love. Setting: Nigeria, the United States, and the United Kingdom. About the author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie is a Nigerian writer, whose works include fiction, nonfiction, and lectures. She is widely recognised as a central figure in postcolonial feminist literature.

title: Dataclysm
author: Christian Rudder
text: Published 2014. Genre: Social Science. Dataclysm explores how our online behaviors and interactions reveal insights into human nature and societal trends. The book analyzes data from various online platforms, particularly focusing on dating, to illustrate how this information can reshape our understanding of behavior and relationships. Rudder presents a compelling argument about the implications of big data on human behavior and social science. Tone and style: irreverent, analytical, engaging. Pacing: methodical, data-driven. Themes: identity, online behavior, data analysis. Setting: contemporary digital landscape. About the author: Christian Rudder is an American technology entrepreneur and writer known for co-founding the online dating service OkCupid and publishing the site's popular blog posts, which offered insights on dating based on data of user behavior. Following OkCupid's sale to the owner of Match.com in 2011, Rudder remained at the company for four years, and in 2014 published the book Dataclysm with further analysis of online dating statistics. He left OkCupid in 2015.

title: The Power of the Dog
author: Don Winslow
text: Published 2006. Genre: Thriller. The Power of the Dog follows DEA agent Art Keller as he navigates the treacherous landscape of the drug trade, facing off against the Barrera brothers who run a powerful drug empire. The narrative spans locations from New York City to Mexico, delving into the lives of various characters, including a high-class hooker and a merciless hitman, all intertwined in the violent world of drug trafficking. The novel explores themes of corruption, betrayal, and the brutal realities of the war on drugs. Tone and style: gritty, fast-paced, intense. Pacing: fast-paced, plot-driven. Themes: corruption, betrayal, drug trade, revenge. Setting: contemporary drug trade in the Americas. About the author: Don Winslow is an American author best known for his crime novels including Savages, The Force and the Cartel Trilogy.

title: The Life and Death of Great American Cities
author: Jane Jacobs
text: Published 1961. Genre: Social Science. Jane Jacobs critiques mid-20th century urban planning policies, arguing that they often disregard the needs of city residents. She emphasizes the importance of vibrant, mixed-use neighborhoods and community engagement in urban design. The book advocates for a more humane and organic approach to city living, challenging the prevailing notions of urban renewal and slum clearance. Tone and style: insightful, analytical, passionate. Pacing: thoughtful, argument-driven. Themes: urban planning, community, city life. Setting: mid-20th century American cities. About the author: Jane Isabel Jacobs was an American-Canadian journalist, author, theorist, and activist who influenced urban studies, sociology, and economics. Her book The Death and Life of Great American Cities (1961) argued that "urban renewal" and "slum clearance" did not respect the needs of city-dwellers.

title: Fortune Smiles
author: Adam Johnson
text:
Published 2015. Genre: Short Stories. Fortune Smiles is a collection of six short stories that explore themes of love, loss, and the intersection of personal and political experiences. The stories include a programmer who finds solace in a digital version of the president while dealing with his wife's illness, and two North Korean defectors navigating their new lives in Seoul. Johnson's narratives often reflect on the impact of technology and natural disasters on human relationships. Tone and style: emotional, inventive, compassionate. Pacing: varied, character-driven. Themes: love, loss, technology, identity, politics. Setting: various locations including North Korea and post-Katrina Louisiana. About the author: Adam Johnson may refer to:Adam Johnson (baseball), American baseball player
Adam Johnson, British classical pianist and conductor
Adam Johnson, Canadian classical conductor
Adam Johnson (cricketer), English cricketer
Adam Johnson (footballer), English footballer
Adam Johnson (1994–2023), American ice hockey player
Adam Johnson (musician), American musician, sound designer and visual artist
Adam Johnson (volleyball) American volleyball player
Adam Johnson (writer), American author
Adam Christian Johnson, American Capitol rioter
Adam R. Johnson, state congressman in the Arkansas House of Representatives
Stovepipe Johnson, brigadier general of the Confederate States of America

author: Ben Lerner
text: Published 2014. Genre: Literary Fiction. In '10:04', the narrator navigates the complexities of life in New York City during a time of social unrest and environmental crisis. He faces a potentially fatal diagnosis, literary success, and the challenge of helping his best friend conceive a child. The novel explores themes of mortality, creativity, and the future amidst a rapidly changing world. Tone and style: introspective, lyrical, contemporary. Pacing: measured, reflective. Themes: mortality, creativity, fatherhood, social unrest. Setting: contemporary New York City. About the author: Benjamin S. Lerner is an American poet, novelist, essayist, and critic. The recipient of fellowships from the Fulbright, Guggenheim, and MacArthur Foundations, Lerner's work has been a finalist for the National Book Award for Poetry, the National Book Critics Circle Award in fiction, and the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction. Lerner teaches at Brooklyn College, where he was named a Distinguished Professor of English in 2016.

title: Station 11
author: Emily St. John Mandel
text: Published 2015-06-02. Genre: Literary Fiction. Station Eleven follows a group of actors and musicians, known as The Traveling Symphony, as they navigate a post-apocalyptic world ravaged by a flu pandemic. The story intertwines their lives with that of a Hollywood actor, Arthur Leander, whose heart attack during a performance marks the beginning of civilization's collapse. Through a non-linear narrative, the novel explores themes of art, humanity, and survival in the face of catastrophe. Tone and style: lyrical, contemplative, character-driven. Pacing: measured, reflective. Themes: art, survival, civilization, memory. Setting: post-apocalyptic Great Lakes region. About the author: Emily St. John Mandel is a Canadian novelist and essayist. She has written six novels, including Station Eleven (2014), The Glass Hotel (2020), and Sea of Tranquility (2022). Station Eleven, which has been translated into 33 languages, has been adapted into a limited series on HBO Max. The Glass Hotel was translated into twenty languages and was selected by Barack Obama as one of his favorite books of 2020. Sea of Tranquility was published in April 2022 and debuted at number three on The New York Times Best Seller list.

title: Fledgling
author: Octavia Butler
text: Published 2005. Genre: Science Fiction. Fledgling follows an amnesiac girl who discovers she is a genetically modified vampire with unique needs and abilities. As she seeks to uncover her past and the threats against her, the novel explores themes of identity and humanity. Butler's work challenges societal norms and delves into issues of race, gender, and belonging. Tone and style: thought-provoking, concise prose. Pacing: slow-burn, character-driven. Themes: identity, otherness, humanity. Setting: contemporary society with speculative elements. About the author: Octavia Estelle Butler was an American science fiction and speculative fiction author who won several awards for her works, including Hugo, Locus, and Nebula awards. In 1995, Butler became the first science-fiction writer to receive a MacArthur Fellowship.

title: The Three Body Problem
author: Cixin Liu
text: Published 2008. Genre: Science Fiction. The Three Body Problem follows a secret military group's attempts to contact extraterrestrial life, which leads to a response from an alien civilization facing its own existential crisis. As news of the impending invasion spreads, humanity is divided between those who wish to ally with the aliens and those who prepare to resist. The novel explores themes of science, philosophy, and the consequences of first contact. Tone and style: thought-provoking, intricate, speculative. Pacing: slow-burn, concept-driven. Themes: first contact, humanity, existential risk. Setting: contemporary China and beyond. About the author: Liu Cixin is a Chinese computer engineer and science fiction writer. In English translations of his works, his name is given as Cixin Liu. He is sometimes called "Da Liu" by his fellow science fiction writers in China.

title: Between the World and Me
author: Ta-Nehisi Coates
text: Published 2015. Genre: Biography & Memoir. Between the World and Me is a personal letter from Ta-Nehisi Coates to his son, exploring the realities of being black in America. It delves into the historical and ongoing impacts of racism, slavery, and segregation, while also reflecting on Coates's own experiences and awakening to these truths. The book combines personal narrative with broader historical context to confront America's racial history and its implications for the future. Tone and style: intimate, reflective, poignant. Pacing: measured, contemplative. Themes: race, identity, history, fatherhood. Setting: contemporary America. About the author: Ta-Nehisi Paul Coates is an American author, journalist, and activist. He gained a wide readership during his time as national correspondent at The Atlantic, where he wrote about cultural, social, and political issues, particularly regarding African Americans and white supremacy. He is politically progressive.

title: Founding Brothers
author: Joseph J Ellis
text: Published 2000. Genre: History. Joseph J. Ellis examines six pivotal moments in early American history that highlight the challenges faced by the new nation. These events include the duel between Burr and Hamilton, a secret dinner that determined the location of the capital, Franklin's petition against slavery, Washington's Farewell Address, Adams's presidency, and the correspondence between Adams and Jefferson later in life. Through these episodes, Ellis explores the complexities of the founding generation's legacy. Tone and style: analytical, engaging, accessible. Pacing: focused, episodic. Themes: founding fathers, political legacy, American history. Setting: late 18th-century United States. About the author: Joseph John-Michael Ellis III is an American historian whose work focuses on the lives and times of the Founding Fathers of the United States. His book American Sphinx: The Character of Thomas Jefferson won a National Book Award in 1997 and Founding Brothers: The Revolutionary Generation won the 2001 Pulitzer Prize for History. Both books were bestsellers.

title: The Boys in the Boat
author: Daniel James Brown
text: Published 2013. Genre: Biography & Memoir. The Boys in the Boat tells the true story of the University of Washington's eight-oar crew team, composed of working-class boys, who triumphed at the 1936 Olympics in Berlin. Led by Joe Rantz, who faced personal hardships, the team defied expectations by defeating elite crews from the East Coast and Great Britain, culminating in a historic victory against the German team. The narrative explores themes of perseverance, camaraderie, and the impact of the Great Depression on their lives. Tone and style: inspirational, narrative nonfiction. Pacing: engaging, character-driven. Themes: perseverance, teamwork, self-discovery. Setting: 1930s America and Berlin. About the author: Daniel James Brown is an American author of narrative nonfiction books.

title: Hillbilly Elegy
author: J. D. Vance
text: Published 2016. Genre: Biography & Memoir. Hillbilly Elegy is a memoir by J.D. Vance that explores his upbringing in a working-class family from the Rust Belt. It examines the struggles of white working-class Americans, particularly focusing on themes of poverty, addiction, and family trauma. Vance reflects on his family's journey from Kentucky to Ohio and his own path to success, highlighting the challenges faced by those trying to achieve upward mobility in America. Tone and style: honest, reflective, personal. Pacing: measured, narrative-driven. Themes: poverty, family trauma, social mobility. Setting: Rust Belt America, primarily Ohio and Kentucky. About the author: James David Vance is an American politician, author, and venture capitalist serving as the 50th vice president of the United States. A member of the Republican Party, he represented the state of Ohio in the United States Senate from 2023 to 2025.

title: Binti
author: Nnedi Okorafor
text: Published 2015. Genre: Science Fiction. Binti is the first of the Himba people to be accepted into Oomza University, the galaxy's top institution. Her journey to the university forces her to confront the cultural sacrifices she must make and the dangers posed by the Meduse, an alien race with a history of conflict with the institution. To survive, Binti must navigate her identity and the wisdom of her heritage while facing unprecedented challenges in a foreign environment. Tone and style: rich, evocative, culturally infused. Pacing: fast-paced, character-driven. Themes: identity, cultural conflict, survival. Setting: futuristic space travel and interstellar academia. About the author: Nnedimma Nkemdili "Nnedi" Okorafor is a Nigerian American writer of science fiction and fantasy for both children and adults. She is best known for her Binti Series and her novels Who Fears Death, Zahrah the Windseeker, Akata Witch, Akata Warrior, Lagoon and Remote Control. She has also written for comics and film.

title: Seveneves
author: Neal Stephenson
text: Published 2015. Genre: Science Fiction. Seveneves explores the catastrophic event that leads to the destruction of Earth and the subsequent efforts of humanity to survive in space. The story follows the challenges faced by the remnants of humanity as they attempt to preserve the human race and rebuild civilization across generations. It delves into themes of science, technology, and the resilience of human ingenuity. Tone and style: epic, speculative, detailed. Pacing: fast-paced, plot-driven. Themes: survival, humanity, technology, resilience. Setting: near-future space and post-apocalyptic Earth. About the author: Neal Town Stephenson is an American writer known for his works of speculative fiction. His novels have been categorized as science fiction, historical fiction, cyberpunk, and baroque.

title: Building a Movement to End the New Jim Crow
author: Daniel Hunter
text:
Published 2015. Genre: Politics & Current Affairs. This book discusses strategies for dismantling the prison industrial complex, which is likened to a modern iteration of the Jim Crow system. Daniel Hunter outlines key organizing principles and provides examples of successful campaigns led by individuals and coalitions in the fight for justice. The focus is on building a movement that can lead to significant societal change. Tone and style: direct, activist-oriented, informative. Pacing: methodical, example-driven. Themes: justice, activism, systemic racism. Setting: contemporary United States. About the author: Daniel Hunter may refer to:Daniel Hunter (musician), founder of Analog Rebellion
Daniel Hunter (volleyball), British volleyball player
Daniel Hunter (swimmer), New Zealand swimmer

title: Democracy for Realists
author: Christopher Achens and Larry Bartels
text: Published 2016. Genre: Politics & Current Affairs. Democracy for Realists critiques the idealistic view of democracy that assumes informed citizens make rational choices at the polls. Instead, Achen and Bartels argue that voters primarily align with social identities and partisan loyalties, often disregarding political issues. The authors use social-scientific evidence to illustrate how elections can hinge on irrelevant factors, suggesting that a more realistic understanding of democracy should center on identity groups and political parties rather than individual voter preferences. Tone and style: analytical, accessible, evidence-based. Pacing: methodical, evidence-driven. Themes: democracy, voter behavior, political identity. Setting: contemporary American political landscape. About the author: Larry Martin Bartels is an American political scientist and the Co-Director of the Center for the Study of Democratic Institutions and Shayne Chair in Public Policy and Social Science at Vanderbilt University. Prior to his appointment at Vanderbilt, Bartels served as the Donald E. Stokes Professor of Public Policy and International Relations and founding director of the Center for the Study of Democratic Politics at the Woodrow Wilson School of Public and International Affairs at Princeton University. He was elected a Member of the American Philosophical Society in 2019.

title: My Brilliant Friend
author: Elena Ferrante
text: Published 2023. Genre: Literary Fiction. My Brilliant Friend follows the complex friendship between two women, Lila and Elena, from their childhood in a poor neighborhood of Naples in the 1950s through their adolescence and into adulthood. The novel explores themes of identity, social change, and the impact of their environment on their lives and relationship. It is the first book in a four-volume series that chronicles their intertwined journeys over nearly sixty years. Tone and style: intimate, evocative, richly detailed. Pacing: slow-burn, character-driven. Themes: friendship, identity, social change. Setting: mid-20th century Naples, Italy. About the author: Elena Ferrante is a pseudonymous Italian novelist. Ferrante's books, originally published in Italian, have been translated into many languages. Her four-book series of Neapolitan Novels are her most widely known works. Time magazine called Ferrante one of the 100 most influential people in 2016.

title: The House of God
author: Samuel Shem
text: Published 1978. Genre: Literary Fiction. The House of God follows a group of medical interns as they navigate the challenges and absurdities of their training in a hospital. Led by a senior resident known as the Fat Man, they confront the grueling demands of their profession, balancing the pressures of life-and-death situations with the need for personal growth and humanity. The novel combines dark humor with a candid portrayal of the medical profession's realities. Tone and style: darkly humorous, candid, raw. Pacing: fast-paced, episodic. Themes: medical training, humanity, resilience, dark comedy. Setting: a hospital in the United States. About the author: Samuel Shem is the pen name of the American psychiatrist Stephen Joseph Bergman. His main works are The House of God and Mount Misery, both fictional but close-to-real first-hand descriptions of the training of doctors in the United States.

title: The Undoing Project
author: Michael Lewis
text: Published 2016. Genre: Biography & Memoir. The Undoing Project explores the groundbreaking work of psychologists Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky, who developed the field of behavioral economics. Their research on human decision-making and cognitive biases has had a profound impact on various domains, including economics, medicine, and public policy. Michael Lewis examines their partnership and the implications of their theories on our understanding of human reasoning and uncertainty. Tone and style: insightful, engaging, analytical. Pacing: methodical, exploratory. Themes: decision-making, cognitive biases, friendship, uncertainty. Setting: modern psychology and economics. About the author: Michael Monroe Lewis is an American author and financial journalist. He has also been a contributing editor to Vanity Fair since 2009, writing mostly on business, finance, and economics. He is known for his nonfiction work, particularly his coverage of financial crises and behavioral finance.

title: Beloved
author: Toni Morrison
text: Published 1987. Genre: Historical Fiction. Beloved tells the story of Sethe, an escaped slave living in Ohio, who is haunted by the traumatic memories of her past at Sweet Home, the plantation where she was enslaved. Eighteen years after her escape, she struggles with her painful history and the ghost of her deceased child, who returns in the form of a mysterious young woman named Beloved. The novel explores themes of memory, trauma, and the enduring impact of slavery on individuals and families. Tone and style: lyrical, haunting, intense. Pacing: slow-burn, character-driven. Themes: slavery, memory, motherhood, trauma. Setting: post-Civil War Ohio. About the author: Chloe Anthony Wofford "Toni" Morrison was an American novelist and editor. She was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1993. Her first novel, The Bluest Eye, was published in 1970. The critically acclaimed Song of Solomon (1977) brought her national attention and won the National Book Critics Circle Award. In 1988, Morrison won the Pulitzer Prize for Beloved (1987). Some of her other notable works include The Bluest Eye (1970), Song of Solomon (1977), Sula (1973), and Recitatif (1983).

title: Oil
author: Vaclav Smil
text: Published 2008. Genre: Science & Technology. Vaclav Smil's "Oil: A Beginner's Guide" explores the significance of oil in modern society, detailing its discovery, uses, and the controversies surrounding it. The book discusses humanity's ongoing dependence on oil and its impact on various aspects of life, including politics and economics. It aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of oil as a resource and its role in shaping the contemporary world. Tone and style: informative, accessible, analytical. Pacing: structured, fact-driven. Themes: energy dependence, environmental impact, economic significance. Setting: global context of oil use and politics. About the author: Vaclav Smil is a Czech-Canadian scientist and policy analyst. He is Distinguished Professor Emeritus in the Faculty of Environment at the University of Manitoba in Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada. His interdisciplinary research interests encompass energy, environmental, food, population, economic, historical and public policy studies. He has also applied these approaches to energy, food and environmental affairs of China.

title: Lexicon
author: Max Barry
text: Published 2013. Genre: Thriller. In 'Lexicon', Emily Ruff is recruited by a secretive organization for her exceptional linguistic skills, while Wil Parke finds himself pursued by the same group after surviving a traumatic event he can't recall. The narrative revolves around the power of words, suggesting that certain words can have lethal effects. As the story unfolds, both characters confront the dangerous implications of language and communication. Tone and style: smart, darkly humorous, fast-paced. Pacing: rapid, suspenseful. Themes: language, power, memory, survival. Setting: contemporary urban environments. About the author: Max Barry is an Australian author and software developer. He also maintains a blog on various topics, including politics.

title: The Art of War
author: Sun Tzu
text: Published 1900. Genre: Other. The Art of War is an ancient Chinese military treatise attributed to Sun Tzu, focusing on various aspects of warfare and strategy. Comprising 13 chapters, it outlines principles of military tactics that have influenced both Eastern and Western thought for centuries. The text is not only significant in military contexts but has also been applied to business and legal strategies. Tone and style: concise, strategic, philosophical. Pacing: structured, analytical. Themes: strategy, warfare, leadership. Setting: ancient China, Warring States period. About the author: Sun Tzu was a Chinese military general, strategist, philosopher, and writer who lived during the Eastern Zhou period. Sun Tzu is traditionally credited as the author of The Art of War, a Classical Chinese text on military strategy from the Warring States period, though the earliest parts of the work probably date to at least a century after him.

title: Capitalist Realism
author: Mark Fisher
text: Published 2009. Genre: Politics & Current Affairs. Mark Fisher's "Capitalist Realism" explores the pervasive belief that capitalism is the only viable political and economic system. The book critiques how this mindset limits our understanding of alternatives and examines the cultural and psychological impacts of living under such a regime. Fisher argues for the necessity of reimagining political possibilities beyond capitalism. Tone and style: critical, analytical, contemporary. Pacing: concise, argumentative. Themes: capitalism, political economy, cultural critique. Setting: contemporary socio-political landscape. About the author: Mark Fisher, also known under his blogging alias k-punk, was an English writer, music critic, political and cultural theorist, philosopher, Marxist and teacher based in the Department of Visual Cultures at Goldsmiths, University of London. He initially achieved acclaim for his blogging as k-punk in the early 2000s, and was known for his writing on radical politics, music, and popular culture.

title: Olive Kitteridge
author: Elizabeth Strout
text: Published 2007. Genre: Literary Fiction. Olive Kitteridge is a collection of interconnected stories centered on the titular character, a retired schoolteacher in Crosby, Maine. The narrative explores her complex relationships with family and townspeople, revealing her struggles with change and her own emotional challenges. Through Olive's experiences, the book delves into themes of human connection, resilience, and the nuances of everyday life. Tone and style: introspective, poignant, character-driven. Pacing: measured, reflective. Themes: identity, change, human connection. Setting: small-town Maine, contemporary. About the author: Elizabeth Strout is an American novelist and author. She is widely known for her works in literary fiction and her descriptive characterization. She was born and raised in Portland, Maine, and her experiences in her youth served as inspiration for her novels—the fictional "Shirley Falls, Maine" is the setting of four of her ten novels.

title: Getting to Yes
author: Roger Fisher and William Ury
text: Published 1981. Genre: Business & Economics. Getting to Yes presents a negotiation strategy that emphasizes reaching mutually acceptable agreements in various conflicts. It teaches key principles such as separating people from the problem, focusing on interests rather than positions, and collaboratively creating options that satisfy both parties. This guide is rooted in the work of the Harvard Negotiation Project and is applicable to personal and professional disputes. Tone and style: practical, straightforward, instructional. Pacing: structured, methodical. Themes: negotiation, conflict resolution, collaboration. Setting: general principles of negotiation in various contexts. About the author: Roger D. Fisher was a Samuel Williston Professor of Law at Harvard Law School and director of the Harvard Negotiation Project.

title: The Grapes of Wrath
author: John Steinbeck
text: Published 1939. Genre: Historical Fiction. The Grapes of Wrath follows the Joad family as they are displaced from their Oklahoma farm during the Great Depression and journey to California in search of a better life. The novel explores themes of injustice, human dignity, and the struggle between the powerful and the powerless. Through their trials, it presents a poignant critique of social and economic inequalities in America. Tone and style: naturalistic, poignant, plainspoken. Pacing: measured, character-driven. Themes: displacement, injustice, human dignity, economic inequality. Setting: 1930s America, primarily Oklahoma and California. About the author: John Ernst Steinbeck was an American writer and novelist. He won the 1962 Nobel Prize in Literature "for his realistic and imaginative writings, combining as they do sympathetic humor and keen social perception". He has been called "a giant of American letters". One of the most widely read authors of the 20th century, he was also an independent journalist and war correspondent during World War II and the Vietnam War.

title: White Rage
author: Carol Anderson
text: Published 2016. Genre: Social Science. White Rage examines the historical patterns of resistance to black progress in America from the Civil War to the present. Carol Anderson argues that every time African Americans have made strides toward equality, there has been a corresponding backlash from white society, manifesting in various forms of institutional racism. The book connects significant historical events and policies that reflect this ongoing struggle. Tone and style: scholarly, urgent, accessible. Pacing: methodical, evidence-driven. Themes: race, systemic racism, historical backlash. Setting: American history from 1865 to present. About the author: Carol Elaine Anderson is an American academic. She is the Charles Howard Candler professor of African American Studies at Emory University. Her research focuses on public policy with regard to race, justice, and equality. In 2023, she was elected to the American Philosophical Society.

title: Lincoln in the Bardo
author: George Saunders
text: Published 2017. Genre: Literary Fiction. Set in February 1862, the novel explores President Abraham Lincoln's grief following the death of his eleven-year-old son, Willie. As Lincoln visits Willie's crypt, the story delves into a supernatural realm called the bardo, where Willie and other spirits navigate their existence and confront their pasts. The narrative blends historical fact with imaginative fiction, addressing themes of love, loss, and the human condition. Tone and style: lyrical, imaginative, poignant. Pacing: meditative, character-driven. Themes: grief, love, mortality, the afterlife. Setting: Civil War-era America, purgatory. About the author: George Saunders is an American writer. He is best known for his short stories and his novel Lincoln in the Bardo (2017), which won the Booker Prize. Saunders's short stories have been published as several collections, including CivilWarLand in Bad Decline (1996) and Tenth of December: Stories (2013).

title: The Shame of the Nation: The Restoration of Aparthied Schooling in America
author: Jonathan Kozol
text: Published 2006-08-01. Genre: Social Science. The Shame of the Nation examines the re-segregation of American schools and the detrimental effects of high-stakes testing on education. Jonathan Kozol highlights the experiences of students, teachers, and community leaders in inner-city schools, revealing the harsh, prison-like conditions imposed on children. He advocates for a return to humane educational practices and challenges the systemic inequalities that persist in the American education system. Tone and style: passionate, urgent, critical. Pacing: methodical, evidence-based. Themes: segregation, education reform, inequality. Setting: contemporary American urban schools. About the author: Jonathan Kozol is an American writer, progressive activist, and educator, best known for his books on public education in the United States.

title: Weapons of Math Destruction
author: Cathy O'Neil
text: Published 2016. Genre: Social Science. Cathy O'Neil explores the impact of algorithms and mathematical models on society, arguing that they often perpetuate inequality and discrimination. She highlights how these unregulated systems influence critical decisions in education, employment, and finance, ultimately undermining democratic values. The book serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of relying on data-driven decision-making without accountability. Tone and style: critical, analytical, accessible. Pacing: methodical, evidence-based. Themes: data ethics, inequality, algorithmic bias. Setting: contemporary society, focusing on data-driven decision-making. About the author: Catherine Helen O'Neil is an American mathematician, data scientist, and author. She is the author of the New York Times best-seller Weapons of Math Destruction, and opinion columns in Bloomberg View. O'Neil was active in the Occupy movement.

title: The Argonauts
author: Maggie Nelson
text: Published 2015. Genre: Biography & Memoir. The Argonauts is a memoir that explores themes of desire, identity, and the complexities of love and language. It centers on Maggie Nelson's relationship with artist Harry Dodge, who has a fluid gender identity, and details her experiences of falling in love and navigating pregnancy. The book blends personal narrative with theoretical reflections, challenging traditional boundaries of autobiography. Tone and style: intimate, reflective, lyrical. Pacing: contemplative, nonlinear. Themes: desire, identity, love, gender fluidity, motherhood. Setting: contemporary exploration of personal and relational identity. About the author: Maggie Nelson is an American writer. She has been described as a genre-busting writer defying classification, working in autobiography, art criticism, theory, feminism, queerness, sexual violence, the history of the avant-garde, aesthetic theory, philosophy, scholarship, and poetry. Nelson received a 2016 MacArthur Fellowship, and several other major awards in the years before that. She is best known for her work of autotheory, The Argonauts (2015).

title: Ready Player One
author: Ernst Cline
text: Published 2008. Genre: Science Fiction. In a dystopian future where reality is bleak, Wade Watts escapes into the OASIS, a massive virtual reality world. After the OASIS's creator dies, he leaves behind a series of puzzles tied to 1980s pop culture, with his fortune and control of the OASIS at stake. Wade must navigate these challenges while facing dangerous rivals who will stop at nothing to win. Tone and style: fast-paced, nostalgic, adventurous. Pacing: fast-paced, quest-driven. Themes: identity, escapism, competition, friendship. Setting: dystopian future, virtual reality. About the author: Ernest Christy Cline is an American science fiction novelist, slam poet and screenwriter. He wrote the novels Ready Player One, Armada, and Ready Player Two, and co-wrote the screenplay for the film adaptation of Ready Player One, directed by Steven Spielberg.

title: The Attention Merchants
author: Tim Wu
text: Published 2016. Genre: Social Science. The Attention Merchants explores the history and impact of advertising and the companies that capture and monetize human attention. Tim Wu examines how these 'attention merchants' have evolved and the implications of their practices on society and individual behavior. The book argues that our attention has become a commodity, influencing not just consumption habits but also our culture and democracy. Tone and style: analytical, engaging, critical. Pacing: methodical, evidence-based. Themes: advertising, consumerism, attention economy. Setting: modern digital landscape. About the author: Timothy Shiou-Ming Wu is an American legal scholar who served as Special Assistant to the President for Technology and Competition Policy at the United States from 2021 to 2023. He is also a professor of law at Columbia University and a contributing opinion writer for The New York Times. He is known legally and academically for significant contributions to antitrust and communications policy, coining the phrase "network neutrality" in his 2003 law journal article, Network Neutrality, Broadband Discrimination. In the late 2010s, Wu was a leading advocate for an antitrust lawsuit directed at the breakup of Facebook.

title: Spin
author: Robet Charles Wilson
text: Published 2005. Genre: Science Fiction. In "Spin," Earth is enveloped by a mysterious membrane that alters the passage of time, causing time to move more slowly on the planet compared to the rest of the universe. The story follows three friends as they navigate the implications of this phenomenon on their lives and relationships. As they grapple with the changes brought about by the Spin, they confront existential questions about humanity's place in the cosmos. Tone and style: thought-provoking, lyrical prose. Pacing: slow-burn, character-driven. Themes: time, friendship, existentialism. Setting: near-future Earth and the cosmos. About the author: Robert Charles Wilson is an American-Canadian science fiction author.

title: What I Talk About When I Talk About Running
author: Haruki Murakami
text: Published 2008. Genre: Biography & Memoir. In this memoir, Haruki Murakami reflects on his dual passions for running and writing, exploring how they influence each other. As he trains for the New York City Marathon, he shares personal anecdotes and insights about the discipline required for both pursuits. The book offers a contemplative look at the nature of creativity and the importance of physical movement in the artistic process. Tone and style: introspective, reflective, candid. Pacing: measured, contemplative. Themes: creativity, discipline, solitude. Setting: personal journey through running and writing. About the author: Haruki Murakami  is a Japanese writer. His novels, essays, and short stories have been best-sellers in Japan and internationally, with his work translated into 50 languages and having sold millions of copies outside Japan. He has received numerous awards for his work, including the Gunzo Prize for New Writers, the World Fantasy Award, the Tanizaki Prize, Yomiuri Prize for Literature, the Frank O'Connor International Short Story Award, the Noma Literary Prize, the Franz Kafka Prize, the Kiriyama Prize for Fiction, the Goodreads Choice Awards for Best Fiction, the Jerusalem Prize, and the Princess of Asturias Awards.

title: Norweigan Wood
author: Haruki Murakami
text: Published 2000. Genre: Literary Fiction. 'Norwegian Wood' follows Toru Watanabe, a college student in Tokyo, as he navigates his complex feelings for two women: the emotionally fragile Naoko and the lively Midori. The story explores themes of love, loss, and the impact of grief, set against the backdrop of 1960s Japan. Toru's relationships are deeply influenced by the memory of his deceased friend, leading him to confront his own emotional struggles. Tone and style: introspective, melancholic, lyrical. Pacing: slow-burn, character-driven. Themes: love, loss, grief, memory. Setting: 1960s Tokyo, Japan. About the author: Haruki Murakami  is a Japanese writer. His novels, essays, and short stories have been best-sellers in Japan and internationally, with his work translated into 50 languages and having sold millions of copies outside Japan. He has received numerous awards for his work, including the Gunzo Prize for New Writers, the World Fantasy Award, the Tanizaki Prize, Yomiuri Prize for Literature, the Frank O'Connor International Short Story Award, the Noma Literary Prize, the Franz Kafka Prize, the Kiriyama Prize for Fiction, the Goodreads Choice Awards for Best Fiction, the Jerusalem Prize, and the Princess of Asturias Awards.

title: Evicted
author: Matthew Desmond
text: Published 2016. Genre: Social Science. Evicted follows the lives of eight families in Milwaukee as they navigate the challenges of housing insecurity and eviction. The book examines the systemic issues surrounding poverty and economic exploitation, highlighting the importance of stable housing for overall well-being. Through personal stories, it sheds light on the struggles faced by those living in precarious conditions and offers insights into potential solutions for these pressing social issues. Tone and style: empathetic, journalistic, insightful. Pacing: measured, narrative-driven. Themes: poverty, housing insecurity, economic exploitation. Setting: contemporary Milwaukee, Wisconsin. About the author: Matthew Desmond is an American sociologist. He is the Maurice P. During Professor of Sociology at Princeton University, where he is also the principal investigator of the Eviction Lab. Desmond was elected to the American Philosophical Society in 2022. He was formerly the John L. Loeb Associate Professor of the Social Sciences at Harvard University.

title: The Black Monday Murders: Volume 1
author: Jonathan Hickman
text: Published 2017-01-25. Genre: Graphic Novel. The Black Monday Murders explores the intersection of magic and finance, revealing a hidden world behind major financial institutions. The story delves into the dark secrets and rituals that influence the stock market and wealth accumulation. This volume collects the first four issues of the series, setting the stage for a deeper investigation into its themes. Tone and style: dark, intricate, noir. Pacing: slow-burn, character-driven. Themes: magic, finance, power, secrecy. Setting: contemporary financial institutions. About the author: Jonathan Hickman is an American comic book writer and artist, best known for his creator-owned series The Nightly News, The Manhattan Projects and East of West, as well as his lengthy stints as a writer on Marvel's Fantastic Four, The Avengers and New Avengers. Hickman's other notable work at Marvel includes the S.H.I.E.L.D. limited series, the creation of the Fantastic Four spin-off title FF, as well as two crossover limited series, Infinity and Secret Wars, both of which acted as centerpieces for the eponymous company-wide crossover storylines.

title: Zero to One
author: Peter Thiel
text: Published 2001. Genre: Business & Economics. In 'Zero to One', Peter Thiel argues that true innovation involves creating something entirely new rather than competing in existing markets. He posits that we are in a period of technological stagnation, and emphasizes the importance of original thinking for entrepreneurs. The book encourages leaders to seek unique solutions and explore uncharted territories in business. Tone and style: provocative, analytical, straightforward. Pacing: focused, argument-driven. Themes: innovation, entrepreneurship, competition, technology. Setting: contemporary business landscape. About the author: Peter Andreas Thiel is a German-American entrepreneur, venture capitalist, and conservative political activist. A co-founder of PayPal (1998), Palantir Technologies (2003), and Founders Fund (2005), he was also the first outside investor in Facebook (2004). According to The New York Times, as of December 2025, Thiel's estimated net worth stood at US$27.5 billion, placing him among the 100 richest individuals in the world.

title: The Unbanking of America
author: Lisa Servon
text: Published 2017. Genre: Business & Economics. This book examines why many Americans are abandoning traditional banks and turning to alternative financial services. Lisa Servon shares insights from her experiences working in check-cashing and payday lending businesses, highlighting the struggles of lower- and middle-income individuals with the banking system. The book also explores innovative financial solutions emerging to address the needs of underserved communities. Tone and style: insightful, critical, engaging. Pacing: methodical, investigative. Themes: economic inequality, banking alternatives, financial justice. Setting: contemporary America, focusing on urban financial systems. About the author: Lisa Servon is an American professor who holds the position of chair of the City and Regional Planning Department at the University of Pennsylvania. She specializes in studies of urban poverty, community development, economic development, and issues of gender. She is one of the primary faculty in the Community and Economic Development concentration. Her research has explored economic insecurity, consumer financial services, and financial justice.

title: Black Flags: The Rise of ISIS
author: Joby Warrick
text: Published 2016-09-06. Genre: History. This book details the origins and rise of ISIS, tracing its roots back to a Jordanian prison and the influence of U.S. foreign policy. It combines operational details with insights from key figures in intelligence and government who recognized the threat posed by this extremist group. Warrick's narrative explores the complex interplay of events and decisions that contributed to the emergence of ISIS as a formidable force. Tone and style: engaging, journalistic, analytical. Pacing: methodical, investigative. Themes: militancy, terrorism, foreign policy. Setting: 20th and 21st-century Middle East and U.S.. About the author: Joby Warrick is an American journalist who has worked for The Washington Post since 1996, mostly writing about the Middle East, diplomacy, and national security. He has also written about the intelligence community, the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and the environment, and has also served as a member of the Post's investigation branch. His work has been recognized with two Pulitzer Prizes.

title: The Power of Habit
author: Charles Duhigg
text: Published 2012. Genre: Business & Economics. The Power of Habit examines the science behind why habits exist and how they can be changed. Charles Duhigg explores various case studies, from corporate environments to social movements, to illustrate how understanding habits can lead to personal and professional transformation. The book argues that by recognizing the mechanisms of habits, individuals can improve their lives and achieve greater success. Tone and style: engaging, informative, narrative-driven. Pacing: structured, evidence-based. Themes: habits, change, productivity, human behavior. Setting: various case studies in contemporary society. About the author: Charles Duhigg is an American journalist and non-fiction author. He was a reporter for The New York Times. He currently writes for The New Yorker Magazine and is the author of three books: The Power of Habit: Why We Do What We Do in Life and Business, Smarter Faster Better and Supercommunicators: How to Unlock the Secret Language of Connection. In 2013, Duhigg was the recipient of the Pulitzer Prize for Explanatory Reporting for a series of ten articles on the business practices of Apple and other technology companies.

title: Bluets
author: Maggie Nelson
text: Published 2009. Genre: Literary Fiction. Bluets is a collection of 240 short pieces that explore the emotional and philosophical significance of the color blue. Through a series of lyrical reflections, Maggie Nelson examines themes of love, loss, and the complexities of human experience. The work blends personal narrative with broader cultural commentary, inviting readers to engage with the color in a deeply introspective way. Tone and style: lyrical, philosophical, introspective. Pacing: fragmented, contemplative. Themes: emotion, color, human experience. Setting: abstract exploration of color and emotion. About the author: Maggie Nelson is an American writer. She has been described as a genre-busting writer defying classification, working in autobiography, art criticism, theory, feminism, queerness, sexual violence, the history of the avant-garde, aesthetic theory, philosophy, scholarship, and poetry. Nelson received a 2016 MacArthur Fellowship, and several other major awards in the years before that. She is best known for her work of autotheory, The Argonauts (2015).

title: The Nix
author: Nathan Hill
text:
Published 2016. Genre: Literary Fiction. The Nix follows the story of Samuel Andresen-Anderson, a college professor whose estranged mother, Faye, resurfaces in his life after decades. As he delves into her past, he uncovers her tumultuous life, which intertwines with themes of family, identity, and the impact of societal issues on personal lives. Tone and style: wry, intricate, character-driven. Pacing: slow-burn, reflective. Themes: family, identity, social critique. Setting: contemporary America, spanning several decades. About the author: Nathan or Nate Hill may refer to:Nate Hill (1966–2012), American football player
Nate Hill (artist), American performance artist
Nathan Hill (writer), author of 2017 novel The Nix
Nathan W. Hill, American historical linguist and Tibetologist

title: Homegoing
author: Yaa Gyasi
text: Published 2016. Genre: Historical Fiction. Homegoing follows the lives of two half-sisters, Effia and Esi, born in 18th-century Ghana. While Effia marries an Englishman and lives in comfort, Esi is captured and sold into slavery, leading to a narrative that spans eight generations and explores the impact of slavery on both sides of the Atlantic. The novel examines the legacy of trauma and memory within families and communities affected by slavery. Tone and style: poignant, lyrical, evocative. Pacing: interwoven, generational. Themes: slavery, identity, generational trauma. Setting: Ghana and the United States across centuries. About the author: Yaa Gyasi is a Ghanaian-American novelist. Her work, most notably her 2016 debut novel Homegoing and her 2020 novel Transcendent Kingdom, features themes of lineage, generational trauma, and Black and African identities. At the age of 26, Gyasi won the National Book Critics Circle's John Leonard Award for Best First Book, the PEN/Hemingway Award for Debut Novel, the National Book Foundation's 5 Under 35 honors for 2016 and the 2017 American Book Award. She was awarded a Vilcek Prize for Creative Promise in Literature in 2020. As of 2019, Gyasi lives in Brooklyn, New York.

title: White Noise
author: Don Delillo
text: Published 1984. Genre: Literary Fiction. Jack Gladney, a professor at a liberal arts college, navigates family life amid an environmental disaster caused by a toxic chemical spill. The novel explores themes of modernity, consumerism, and the pervasive nature of fear in contemporary society. Tone and style: satirical, darkly humorous, fragmented. Pacing: measured, reflective. Themes: consumerism, mortality, family dynamics, modernity. Setting: contemporary Middle America. About the author: Donald Richard DeLillo is an American novelist, short story writer, playwright, screenwriter and essayist. His works have covered subjects as diverse as consumerism, nuclear war, the complexities of language, art, television, the advent of the Digital Age, mathematics, politics, economics and sports.

title: Mistborn: The Last Empire
author: Brian Sanderson
text: Published 2017. Genre: Fantasy. In a world where a Dark Lord has triumphed, a young street urchin named Vin discovers her powerful abilities as a Mistborn, a rare type of magic user. She is drawn into a rebellion against the oppressive regime and must navigate complex political intrigue and personal loyalties. As she learns to harness her powers, she faces the realities of betrayal and the consequences of her actions in a struggle for freedom. Tone and style: epic, immersive, character-driven. Pacing: fast-paced, action-oriented. Themes: oppression, rebellion, power, identity. Setting: a dystopian world ruled by a Dark Lord. About the author: Brandon Winn Sanderson is an American author of high fantasy, science fiction, and young adult books. His best known novels include the Mistborn series and The Stormlight Archive, which are set in the "Cosmere", a fictional universe. Outside of the Cosmere, he has written several young adult and juvenile series including The Reckoners, the Skyward series, and the Alcatraz series. He is also known for finishing author Robert Jordan's high fantasy series The Wheel of Time. Sanderson has created two graphic novels, White Sand and Dark One.

title: Unfamiliar Fishes
author: Sarah Vowell
text: Published 2011. Genre: History. Unfamiliar Fishes explores the history of Hawaii and the influence of New England missionaries who arrived in the early 1800s. The book examines how these missionaries sought to transform the islands into a reflection of their own cultural values. Vowell combines historical analysis with personal narrative to highlight the complexities of this cultural encounter. Tone and style: witty, insightful, conversational. Pacing: engaging, anecdotal. Themes: cultural transformation, colonialism, history. Setting: 19th-century Hawaii. About the author: Sarah Jane Vowell is an American historian, writer, journalist, radio personality, social commentator, and actress. She has written seven nonfiction books on American history and culture. Vowell was a contributing editor for the radio program This American Life on Public Radio International from 1996 to 2008, where she produced commentaries and documentaries. She was the voice of Violet Parr in the 2004 animated film The Incredibles and its 2018 sequel.

title: The Checklist Manifesto
author: Atul Gawande
text: Published 2010. Genre: Health & Wellness. In 'The Checklist Manifesto', Atul Gawande explores the challenges of modern complexity in various fields, particularly in medicine. He argues that the use of checklists can significantly reduce errors and improve outcomes by breaking down complicated tasks into manageable steps. Gawande illustrates this concept through examples from different industries, showing how checklists can enhance efficiency and safety. Tone and style: insightful, analytical, clear. Pacing: methodical, evidence-based. Themes: complexity, error reduction, efficiency. Setting: various professional fields including medicine, aviation, and construction. About the author: Atul Atmaram Gawande is an American surgeon, writer, and public health researcher. He practices general and endocrine surgery at Brigham and Women's Hospital in Boston, Massachusetts. He is a professor in the Department of Health Policy and Management at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health and the Samuel O. Thier Professor of Surgery at Harvard Medical School.

title: American Pastoral
author: Philip Roth
text: Published 1997. Genre: Literary Fiction. American Pastoral follows Seymour 'Swede' Levov, a successful businessman and former high school athlete, whose idyllic life in post-war America unravels during the social upheaval of the 1960s. As his daughter becomes involved in radical political activism, Swede grapples with the loss of his American dream and the disintegration of his family. The novel explores themes of identity, societal change, and the complexities of the American experience. Tone and style: introspective, poignant, richly detailed. Pacing: measured, character-driven. Themes: identity, family, societal change. Setting: post-war America, 1960s. About the author: Philip Milton Roth was an American novelist and short-story writer. Roth's fiction—often set in his birthplace of Newark, New Jersey—is known for its intensely autobiographical character, for philosophically and formally blurring the distinction between reality and fiction, for its "sensual, ingenious style" and for its provocative explorations of Jewish and American identity. He first gained attention with the 1959 short story collection Goodbye, Columbus, which won the U.S. National Book Award for Fiction. Ten years later, he published the bestseller Portnoy's Complaint. Nathan Zuckerman, Roth's literary alter ego, narrates several of his books. A fictionalized Roth narrates some of his others, such as the alternate history The Plot Against America.

title: The Opposite of Loneliness
author: Marina Keegan
text:
Published 2014. Genre: Literary Fiction. The Opposite of Loneliness is a posthumous collection of essays and stories by Marina Keegan that explores the hopes, uncertainties, and aspirations of her generation. Written shortly before her untimely death, the pieces reflect on youth, possibility, and the human experience, resonating deeply with readers. The collection includes her notable essay that gained widespread attention and articulates the universal struggle of finding one's path in life. Tone and style: reflective, poignant, youthful. Pacing: varied, contemplative. Themes: youth, aspiration, loss, possibility. Setting: contemporary America. About the author: 
Marina Evelyn Keegan was an American author, playwright, and journalist. She is best known for her essay "The Opposite of Loneliness," which went viral and was viewed over 1.4 million times in 98 countries after her death in a car crash while traveling home as a passenger just five days after she graduated magna cum laude from Yale University.

title: The Shipping News
author: Anne Proulx
text: Published 1993. Genre: Literary Fiction. Quoyle, a struggling newspaper hack, returns to his family's ancestral home in Newfoundland with his two daughters to rebuild their lives. As they navigate their new surroundings, they confront their past traumas and the challenges of their new environment, ultimately seeking connection and healing. Tone and style: lyrical, evocative, character-driven. Pacing: slow-burn, character-driven. Themes: family, trauma, identity, resilience. Setting: contemporary Newfoundland. About the author: Edna Ann Proulx is an American novelist, short story writer, and journalist. She has written most frequently as Annie Proulx but has also used the names E. Annie Proulx and E. A. Proulx.

title: Bobos in Paradise
author: David Brooks
text: Published 2000. Genre: Social Science. David Brooks explores the cultural landscape of contemporary upper-class Americans, whom he labels 'Bobos.' This term describes individuals who blend bourgeois capitalist values with bohemian ideals, reflecting the complexities of modern consumerism and lifestyle choices in the information age. Tone and style: witty, analytical, engaging. Pacing: insightful, reflective. Themes: consumerism, identity, cultural values. Setting: contemporary American society. About the author: David Brooks may refer to:

title: Pachinko
author: Min Jin Lee
text: Published 2017. Genre: Historical Fiction. Pachinko follows the life of Sunja, a young Korean woman who becomes pregnant by a wealthy married man and chooses to marry a sickly minister instead, leading her to Japan. The novel spans four generations of her family as they navigate the challenges of identity, belonging, and survival in a foreign land. It explores themes of love, sacrifice, and ambition against the backdrop of 20th-century Japanese history. Tone and style: richly detailed, emotionally resonant. Pacing: measured, character-driven. Themes: identity, immigration, family, sacrifice. Setting: 20th-century Korea and Japan. About the author: Min Jin Lee is a Korean American author based in Harlem, New York City; her work frequently deals with the Korean diaspora. She is best known for writing Free Food for Millionaires (2007) and Pachinko (2017), a finalist for the National Book Award, and runner-up for the Dayton Literary Peace Prize. In 2019, Lee became a writer-in-residence at Amherst College in Massachusetts. Her upcoming third novel in her Korean quartet, titled American Hagwon, will be released on September 29, 2026.

title: A Picture of Dorian Gray
author: Oscar Wilde
text: Published 1890. Genre: Literary Fiction. A Picture of Dorian Gray tells the story of a young man, Dorian Gray, who becomes enamored with his own portrait and makes a Faustian bargain to remain eternally youthful and beautiful. As he indulges in a life of hedonism and moral decay, only his portrait reveals the consequences of his actions, reflecting the corruption of his soul. The novel critiques the superficiality and moral hypocrisy of Victorian society. Tone and style: darkly ironic, elegant prose. Pacing: slow-burn, character-driven. Themes: beauty, morality, hedonism, corruption. Setting: Victorian England. About the author: Oscar Fingal O'Fflahertie Wills Wilde was an Irish author, poet and playwright. After writing in different literary styles throughout the 1880s, he became one of the most popular and influential dramatists in London in the early 1890s. He was a key figure in the emerging Aestheticism movement of the late 19th century and is widely regarded as the greatest playwright of the Victorian era. Wilde is best known for his Gothic novel The Picture of Dorian Gray (1890), his epigrams, plays and bedtime stories for children, as well as his criminal conviction in 1895 for gross indecency and for practicing homosexual acts.

title: Men Without Women
author: Haruki Murakami
text: Published 2017. Genre: Short Stories. Men Without Women is a collection of seven stories by Haruki Murakami that explores the lives of men who find themselves alone, reflecting on their relationships with women. The characters include a lovesick doctor, an actor, and even Kafka's Gregor Samsa, each navigating themes of loneliness and longing. The stories blend humor and pathos, characteristic of Murakami's writing style. Tone and style: wry, introspective, poignant. Pacing: varied, reflective. Themes: loneliness, relationships, identity. Setting: contemporary Japan. About the author: Haruki Murakami  is a Japanese writer. His novels, essays, and short stories have been best-sellers in Japan and internationally, with his work translated into 50 languages and having sold millions of copies outside Japan. He has received numerous awards for his work, including the Gunzo Prize for New Writers, the World Fantasy Award, the Tanizaki Prize, Yomiuri Prize for Literature, the Frank O'Connor International Short Story Award, the Noma Literary Prize, the Franz Kafka Prize, the Kiriyama Prize for Fiction, the Goodreads Choice Awards for Best Fiction, the Jerusalem Prize, and the Princess of Asturias Awards.

title: Built
author: Roma Agrawal
text: Published 2018. Genre: Science & Technology. In 'Built', structural engineer Roma Agrawal explores the evolution of construction, from ancient mud huts to modern skyscrapers. She discusses the engineering principles behind iconic structures like the Pantheon and the Eiffel Tower, while sharing personal stories and historical insights. The book highlights the importance of engineering in our daily lives and how it shapes the built environment around us. Tone and style: informative, engaging, accessible. Pacing: methodical, narrative-driven. Themes: engineering, architecture, innovation. Setting: global construction history and modern urban environments. About the author: Roma Agrawal is an Indian-British chartered structural engineer based in London. She has worked on several major engineering projects, including the Shard. Agrawal is also an author and a diversity campaigner, championing women in engineering.

title: Severance
author: Ling Ma
text: Published 2018. Genre: Literary Fiction. Severance follows Candace Chen, a millennial office worker in Manhattan who is deeply entrenched in her routine. As a plague known as Shen Fever spreads and society begins to collapse, Candace remains unaffected and continues her solitary existence, documenting the deserted city as she grapples with her past and the loss of her parents. Tone and style: contemporary, reflective, ironic. Pacing: slow-burn, character-driven. Themes: isolation, routine, societal collapse, grief. Setting: post-apocalyptic New York City. About the author: Ling Ma is a Chinese American novelist and professor at the University of Chicago. Her first book, Severance (2018), won a 2018 Kirkus Prize and was listed as a New York Times Notable Book of 2018 and shortlisted for the PEN/Hemingway Award. Her second book, Bliss Montage (2022), won the National Book Critics Circle Award for Fiction and The Story Prize. She is a 2024 MacArthur Fellow.

title: The Gone World
author: Tom Sweterlitsch
text: Published 2018. Genre: Science Fiction. In 1997, special agent Shannon Moss investigates the murder of a Navy SEAL's family and the disappearance of his teenage daughter. As she delves into the case, she learns that the SEAL was involved in time travel aboard a lost spaceship, leading her to explore potential futures to find the girl and prevent a catastrophic event. The story intertwines elements of crime, time travel, and the survival of humanity. Tone and style: tense, thought-provoking, dark. Pacing: fast-paced, plot-driven. Themes: time travel, fate, humanity. Setting: 1997 western Pennsylvania and various futures. About the author: Tom Sweterlitsch is an American author who has published the novels Tomorrow and Tomorrow and The Gone World.

title: Why Buddhism Is True
author: Robin Wright
text: Published 2017-08-08. Genre: Self-Help & Personal Development. In 'Why Buddhism Is True', Robert Wright explores how Buddhist practices, particularly meditation, can help individuals manage negative emotions like anxiety and hatred. He argues that these practices can enhance one's appreciation for beauty and foster a deeper connection with others. The book combines insights from psychology and philosophy to present a case for the relevance of Buddhism in contemporary life. Tone and style: insightful, engaging, analytical. Pacing: thoughtful, reflective. Themes: mindfulness, mental health, philosophy of religion. Setting: modern psychological context. About the author: Robert Wright is an American author and journalist known for his wide-ranging interests in philosophy, society, science, history, politics, international relations, and religion. He has published five books: Three Scientists and Their Gods: Looking for Meaning in an Age of Information (1988), The Moral Animal (1994), Nonzero: The Logic of Human Destiny (1999), The Evolution of God (2009), and Why Buddhism is True (2017). Wright has taught at Princeton University and the University of Pennsylvania; more recently, in 2019 he was Visiting Professor of Science and Religion at Union Theological Seminary, New York.

title: Why We Sleep
author: Matthew Walker
text: Published 2017. Genre: Health & Wellness. Why We Sleep explores the significance of sleep and its impact on our physical and mental health. Matthew Walker, a neuroscientist, discusses the functions of sleep, including its role in learning, emotional regulation, and overall well-being. He presents scientific findings on the consequences of sleep deprivation and offers practical advice for improving sleep quality. Tone and style: clear, engaging, scientific. Pacing: methodical, research-driven. Themes: sleep, health, neuroscience, well-being. Setting: contemporary scientific research on sleep. About the author: Matthew Walker may refer to:

title: Sour Heart
author: Jenny Zhang
text:
Published 2017. Genre: Short Stories. Sour Heart is a collection of stories that explores the experiences of Chinese American girls growing up in New York City. The narratives delve into themes of adolescence, family dynamics, and the immigrant experience, often through darkly humorous and poignant lenses. The stories range from the struggles of fitting in at school to the complexities of cultural identity and familial expectations. Tone and style: darkly humorous, intimate. Pacing: varied, character-driven. Themes: adolescence, immigrant experience, family, identity. Setting: contemporary New York City and historical Shanghai. About the author: Jenny Zhang may refer to:Jenny Zhang (actress), Chinese actress and singer
Jenny Zhang (chemist), Chinese Australian chemist
Jenny Zhang (writer), American writer, poet, and essayist
Jenny Tinghui Zhang (writer), American writer

title: Fox 8
author: George Saunders
text: Published 2013. Genre: Literary Fiction. Fox 8 is a story about a fox who learns to communicate in human language after his home is destroyed by humans building a mall. He writes a letter to humans, expressing his confusion and sorrow over their actions and questioning their cruelty. The narrative explores themes of communication, empathy, and the impact of human development on nature. Tone and style: whimsical, poignant, satirical. Pacing: measured, reflective. Themes: communication, empathy, environmental destruction. Setting: contemporary suburban landscape. About the author: George Saunders is an American writer. He is best known for his short stories and his novel Lincoln in the Bardo (2017), which won the Booker Prize. Saunders's short stories have been published as several collections, including CivilWarLand in Bad Decline (1996) and Tenth of December: Stories (2013).

title: The Remains of the Day
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
text: Published 1989. Genre: Literary Fiction. The Remains of the Day follows Stevens, an aging butler at Darlington Hall, as he takes a road trip through the English countryside in 1956. During this journey, he reflects on his life of service, his relationship with the housekeeper Miss Kenton, and the choices he made that shaped his identity. The novel explores themes of duty, regret, and the passage of time. Tone and style: elegant, introspective, restrained. Pacing: slow-burn, reflective. Themes: duty, regret, memory, class. Setting: post-World War II England. About the author: Sir Kazuo Ishiguro  is a Japanese-British novelist, screenwriter, musician, and short-story writer. He is one of the most critically acclaimed contemporary fiction authors writing in English, having been awarded several major literary prizes, including the 2017 Nobel Prize in Literature. In its citation, the Swedish Academy described Ishiguro as a writer "who, in novels of great emotional force, has uncovered the abyss beneath our illusory sense of connection with the world".

title: The Marriage Plot
author: Jeffrey Eugenides
text: Published 2011. Genre: Literary Fiction. The Marriage Plot follows Madeleine Hanna, an English major in the early 1980s, as she navigates her final year of college. Caught in a love triangle with the charismatic Leonard and the devoted Mitchell, Madeleine grapples with her romantic ideals influenced by classic literature versus the complexities of real-life relationships. The novel explores themes of love, identity, and the transition into adulthood with wit and insight. Tone and style: witty, ironic, contemporary. Pacing: character-driven, reflective. Themes: love, identity, literature, adulthood. Setting: 1980s college campus in the US. About the author: Jeffrey Kent Eugenides is an American author. He has written numerous short stories and essays, as well as three novels: The Virgin Suicides (1993), Middlesex (2002), and The Marriage Plot (2011). The Virgin Suicides served as the basis of the 1999 film of the same name, while Middlesex received the 2003 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction in addition to being a finalist for the National Book Critics Circle Award, the International Dublin Literary Award, and France's Prix Médicis.

title: The Idiot
author: Elif Batuman
text: Published 1969. Genre: Literary Fiction. The Idiot follows Selin, a Turkish-American student, as she navigates her freshman year at Harvard in 1995. Through her correspondence with an older mathematics student named Ivan and her experiences in Europe, Selin explores themes of identity, love, and the complexities of becoming a writer. The novel captures the confusion and excitement of young adulthood with humor and introspection. Tone and style: witty, introspective, conversational. Pacing: measured, character-driven. Themes: identity, love, self-discovery. Setting: 1990s Harvard and Europe. About the author: Elif Batuman is an American author, academic, and journalist. She is the author of three books: a memoir, The Possessed (2010), the novel The Idiot (2017), which was a finalist for the 2018 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction, and Either/Or (2022). Batuman is a staff writer for The New Yorker.

title: Middlesex
author: Jeffrey Eugenides
text: Published 2002. Genre: Literary Fiction. Middlesex follows the life of Calliope Stephanides, who grows up in a Greek-American family in Detroit. As Callie navigates her adolescence at a girls' school, she grapples with her identity and discovers that she is intersex due to a genetic mutation. The novel explores themes of gender, identity, and the immigrant experience across generations. Tone and style: introspective, lyrical, rich prose. Pacing: measured, character-driven. Themes: identity, gender, immigration. Setting: 20th-century Detroit and Greece. About the author: Jeffrey Kent Eugenides is an American author. He has written numerous short stories and essays, as well as three novels: The Virgin Suicides (1993), Middlesex (2002), and The Marriage Plot (2011). The Virgin Suicides served as the basis of the 1999 film of the same name, while Middlesex received the 2003 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction in addition to being a finalist for the National Book Critics Circle Award, the International Dublin Literary Award, and France's Prix Médicis.

title: The Order of the Day
author: Éric Vuillard
text: Published 2018-09-25. Genre: History. The Order of the Day examines the events leading up to Nazi Germany's annexation of Austria, focusing on a secret meeting between industrialists and Nazi officials. It reveals the manipulation, intimidation, and greed that facilitated this political maneuvering, contrasting the public narrative of strength with the reality of a flawed and chaotic process. Vuillard's work serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of complacency in the face of authoritarianism. Tone and style: analytical, engaging, critical. Pacing: measured, detailed. Themes: manipulation, power, complicity. Setting: 1930s Germany and Austria. About the author: Éric Vuillard is a French writer and film director. He has made two films, L'homme qui marche and Mateo Falcone, the latter based on the story Mateo Falcone by Prosper Merimee. He is the author of Conquistadors (2009) which won the Prix de l'inaperçu in 2010. He won the Prix Goncourt in 2017 for L'Ordre du jour.

title: Four Futures
author: Peter Frase
text: Published 2016. Genre: Politics & Current Affairs. Four Futures explores potential societal structures that could emerge as capitalism evolves due to technological and environmental changes. Peter Frase analyzes four distinct futures: communism, rentism, socialism, and exterminism, using speculative fiction to illustrate these possibilities. The book discusses the implications of a resurgent Left and the consequences of its failure. Tone and style: analytical, speculative, engaging. Pacing: methodical, thought-provoking. Themes: capitalism, technology, future societies. Setting: contemporary global context.

title: Green Metropolis
author: David Owen
text: Published 2009. Genre: Social Science. David Owen argues that densely populated urban areas, contrary to popular belief, are more environmentally sustainable than spread-out suburban or rural living. He uses Manhattan as a case study, highlighting how its residents consume less energy and produce fewer greenhouse gases than those in less populated areas. The book challenges the notion that ecological living equates to rural lifestyles, advocating instead for urban density as a solution to environmental issues. Tone and style: engaging, analytical, thought-provoking. Pacing: methodical, evidence-based. Themes: urban living, environmental sustainability, resource consumption. Setting: contemporary urban America. About the author: David Anthony Llewellyn Owen, Baron Owen, is a British politician and physician. He served as Foreign Secretary in the Labour government of James Callaghan from 1977 to 1979, becoming the youngest person appointed to the position since 1935, and later led the Social Democratic Party (SDP). He was a Member of Parliament for 26 years, from 1966 to 1992.

title: The Mote in God's Eye
author: Larry Niven and Jerry Pournelle
text: Published 1974. Genre: Science Fiction. The Mote in God's Eye explores first contact with an alien species known as the Moties, who possess advanced technology but have a complex social structure. The story follows a human crew sent to investigate the Moties, leading to profound questions about communication, trust, and the nature of intelligence. As the humans interact with the Moties, they face challenges that test their understanding of both themselves and the aliens. Tone and style: thought-provoking, detailed, speculative. Pacing: measured, character-driven. Themes: first contact, intelligence, communication, trust. Setting: near-future space, alien civilization.
