Published 1979. Genre: Espionage/Spy. In 'Smiley's People', George Smiley is reluctantly pulled from retirement to investigate the murder of an old acquaintance. As he delves into the case, he uncovers a web of espionage involving a mysterious photograph and a promise made to a dying woman. The novel explores themes of loyalty, betrayal, and the moral complexities of intelligence work. Tone and style: sophisticated, morally ambiguous. Pacing: measured, methodical. Themes: loyalty, betrayal, moral ambiguity. Setting: Cold War Europe, primarily London and Paris. About the author: David John Moore Cornwell, known by his pen name John le Carré, was an English author. 
Many of his espionage novels have been adapted for film or television. He has been described as a "sophisticated, morally ambiguous writer", and is considered one of the greatest novelists of the postwar era. During the 1950s and 1960s, he worked for both the Security Service (MI5) and the Secret Intelligence Service (MI6). Near the end of his life, le Carré became an Irish citizen.

title: The Black Echo
author: Michael Connelly
text:
Published 1992. Genre: Mystery. Harry Bosch, an LAPD detective, investigates the murder of a fellow Vietnam veteran, which becomes deeply personal for him. As he delves into the case, he confronts both external enemies and his own department's politics, forcing him to grapple with the themes of justice versus vengeance. The investigation leads him through a dangerous underbelly of Los Angeles, where he must rely on his instincts to survive. Tone and style: gritty, suspenseful, straightforward. Pacing: fast-paced, plot-driven. Themes: justice, vengeance, trauma, loyalty. Setting: Los Angeles, contemporary. About the author: Michael Joseph Connelly is an American author of detective novels and other crime fiction, notably those featuring LAPD Detective Hieronymus "Harry" Bosch and criminal defense attorney Mickey Haller, including 10 with both those characters. 
Connelly is the bestselling author of 42 novels and one work of non-fiction, with over 74 million copies of his books sold worldwide and translated into 40 languages. His first novel, The Black Echo, won the Mystery Writers of America Edgar Award for Best First Novel in 1992. In 2002, Clint Eastwood directed and starred in the movie adaptation of Connelly's 1997 novel, Blood Work. In March 2011, the movie adaptation of Connelly's novel The Lincoln Lawyer starred Matthew McConaughey as Mickey Haller. Connelly was the President of the Mystery Writers of America from 2003 to 2004.

title: Damascus Station
author: David McCloskey
text: Published 2021. Genre: Espionage/Spy. In 'Damascus Station', a CIA officer and his recruit navigate the complexities of espionage in Syria as they pursue a dangerous assassin. The story explores the challenges of intelligence work in a volatile environment, highlighting themes of loyalty and betrayal. As they delve deeper into their mission, they confront moral dilemmas and the harsh realities of their profession. Tone and style: tense, realistic, suspenseful. Pacing: fast-paced, action-driven. Themes: espionage, loyalty, betrayal. Setting: contemporary Syria. About the author: David McCloskey is an American writer of spy fiction and podcast host. He is a former staff member of the Central Intelligence Agency.

title: The Story of a New Name
author: Elena Ferrante
text: Published 2019. Genre: Literary Fiction. The Story of a New Name follows the evolving friendship between Lila and Elena, two women from post-WWII Naples, Italy. As Lila navigates the challenges of marriage and family business, Elena pursues her education and seeks a life beyond their neighborhood. Their complex bond serves as both a source of strength and a reflection of their individual struggles with love, jealousy, and personal freedom. Tone and style: intense, emotional, richly detailed. Pacing: character-driven, reflective. Themes: friendship, identity, love, jealousy, personal growth. Setting: post-WWII Naples, Italy. About the author: Elena Ferrante is a pseudonymous Italian novelist. Ferrante's books, originally published in Italian, have been translated into many languages. Her four-book series of Neapolitan Novels are her most widely known works. Time magazine called Ferrante one of the 100 most influential people in 2016.

title: The Wright Brothers
author: David McCullough
text: Published 2015. Genre: Biography & Memoir. This biography details the lives of Wilbur and Orville Wright, the bicycle mechanics who invented the first successful powered airplane. It explores their determination, ingenuity, and the challenges they faced in achieving human flight. The book also highlights the role of their sister, Katharine, in supporting their endeavors. Tone and style: engaging, informative, narrative-driven. Pacing: well-paced, detailed. Themes: innovation, perseverance, family support. Setting: early 20th-century America, primarily North Carolina. About the author: David Gaub McCullough was an American popular historian and author. He was a two-time winner of both the Pulitzer Prize and the National Book Award. In 2006, he was given the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the United States' highest civilian award.

title: The Black Ice
author: Michael Connelly
text:
Published 1993. Genre: Mystery. Detective Harry Bosch investigates the death of an LAPD narcotics officer, initially ruled a suicide. His inquiry leads him through a series of drug-related murders that stretch across the Mexico border. As Bosch uncovers dangerous connections, he realizes he may become a target in a deadly game. Tone and style: gritty, suspenseful, straightforward. Pacing: fast-paced, plot-driven. Themes: justice, corruption, danger. Setting: Los Angeles and Mexico border. About the author: Michael Joseph Connelly is an American author of detective novels and other crime fiction, notably those featuring LAPD Detective Hieronymus "Harry" Bosch and criminal defense attorney Mickey Haller, including 10 with both those characters. 
Connelly is the bestselling author of 42 novels and one work of non-fiction, with over 74 million copies of his books sold worldwide and translated into 40 languages. His first novel, The Black Echo, won the Mystery Writers of America Edgar Award for Best First Novel in 1992. In 2002, Clint Eastwood directed and starred in the movie adaptation of Connelly's 1997 novel, Blood Work. In March 2011, the movie adaptation of Connelly's novel The Lincoln Lawyer starred Matthew McConaughey as Mickey Haller. Connelly was the President of the Mystery Writers of America from 2003 to 2004.

title: Call for the Dead
author: Jon La Carré
text:
Published 1961. Genre: Espionage/Spy. In 'Call for the Dead', George Smiley, an intelligence officer, investigates the apparent suicide of Samuel Fennan, a former agent he had recently interviewed. As Smiley delves deeper, he uncovers layers of deception and intrigue within the Cold War espionage landscape. This novel marks the beginning of Smiley's complex character and le Carré's exploration of moral ambiguity in the world of spies. Tone and style: sophisticated, morally ambiguous. Pacing: measured, methodical. Themes: espionage, betrayal, moral ambiguity. Setting: Cold War Europe. About the author: David John Moore Cornwell, known by his pen name John le Carré, was an English author. 
Many of his espionage novels have been adapted for film or television. He has been described as a "sophisticated, morally ambiguous writer", and is considered one of the greatest novelists of the postwar era. During the 1950s and 1960s, he worked for both the Security Service (MI5) and the Secret Intelligence Service (MI6). Near the end of his life, le Carré became an Irish citizen.

title: Digital Minimalism
author: Cal Newport
text: Published 2019. Genre: Self-Help & Personal Development. Digital Minimalism explores the philosophy of using technology in a more intentional and meaningful way. Cal Newport argues for a thoughtful approach to digital tools, emphasizing the importance of disconnecting from distractions to enhance personal fulfillment. The book outlines practical strategies for reducing digital clutter and re-establishing a connection with offline activities, ultimately guiding readers to align their technology use with their values and goals. Tone and style: practical, insightful, engaging. Pacing: methodical, structured. Themes: technology, mindfulness, personal fulfillment. Setting: contemporary digital landscape. About the author: Calvin C. Newport is an American nonfiction author and full time professor of computer science at Georgetown University. He is known for his writings about attention management in the digital age.

title: The Singapore Grip
author: J.G. Farrell
text: Published 1978. Genre: Historical Fiction. Set in Singapore on the brink of World War II, the novel follows Walter Blackett, the head of a powerful British firm, as he navigates the complexities of colonial life. Amidst labor strikes and personal entanglements, Blackett's world is challenged by the impending collapse of the British Empire. The story intertwines themes of love, business, and the socio-political upheaval of the time. Tone and style: darkly comedic, satirical. Pacing: slow-burn, character-driven. Themes: colonialism, class struggle, impending change. Setting: pre-war Singapore, 1939. About the author: James Gordon Farrell was an English-born novelist of Irish descent. He gained prominence for a series of novels known as "the Empire Trilogy", which deal with the political and human consequences of British colonial rule.

title: The Lost City: The Forgotten Virtues of Community in America
author: Alan Ehrenhalt
text: Published 1996-08-23. Genre: Social Science. The Lost City explores the concept of community in America, focusing on life in the 1950s and the changes that followed in subsequent decades. Alan Ehrenhalt examines three neighborhoods in Chicago, highlighting how local institutions like churches and civic leaders shaped social cohesion. He argues that the rejection of authority and the rise of personal choice have eroded community bonds, and suggests that lessons from the past could help restore a sense of belonging today. Tone and style: analytical, evocative, narrative. Pacing: measured, reflective. Themes: community, authority, nostalgia, social compact. Setting: 1950s America, primarily Chicago. About the author: Alan Ehrenhalt is an American journalist and non-fiction author.

title: The Long Goodbye
author: Raymond Chandler
text: Published 1953. Genre: Mystery. In 'The Long Goodbye', private detective Philip Marlowe becomes embroiled in a complex case involving his friend Terry Lennox, who is suspected of murdering his wife. As Marlowe investigates, he encounters a variety of characters, including an alcoholic writer and a gangster, leading him deeper into a web of deception and moral ambiguity. The novel explores themes of friendship, betrayal, and the darker sides of human nature. Tone and style: hard-boiled, cynical, gritty. Pacing: measured, character-driven. Themes: friendship, betrayal, moral ambiguity. Setting: mid-20th century Los Angeles. About the author: Raymond Thornton Chandler was an American-British novelist and screenwriter. In 1932, at age 44, Chandler became a detective fiction writer after losing his job as an oil company executive during the Great Depression. His first short story, "Blackmailers Don't Shoot", was published in 1933 in Black Mask, a pulp magazine. His first novel, The Big Sleep, was published in 1939. In addition to his short stories, Chandler published seven novels during his lifetime. All but Playback have been made into motion pictures, some more than once.

title: Red Harvest
author: Dashiell Hammett
text: Published 1929. Genre: Mystery. In "Red Harvest," a nameless detective arrives in the corrupt town of Personville to clean up the rampant crime and moral decay. The narrative unfolds as he navigates the treacherous landscape of betrayal and violence, employing ruthless tactics to confront the city's criminal elements. Hammett's work is characterized by its gritty realism and sharp dialogue, reflecting the chaotic atmosphere of Prohibition-era America. Tone and style: gritty, terse, hard-boiled. Pacing: fast-paced, plot-driven. Themes: corruption, moral ambiguity, crime. Setting: Prohibition-era America, fictional Personville. About the author: Samuel Dashiell Hammett was an American writer of hard-boiled detective novels and short stories. He was also a screenwriter and political activist. Among the characters he created are Sam Spade, Nick and Nora Charles, The Continental Op and the comic strip character Secret Agent X-9.

title: The Maltese Falcon
author: Dashiell Hammett
text: Published 1929. Genre: Mystery. The Maltese Falcon follows private detective Sam Spade as he becomes embroiled in a dangerous quest for a valuable statuette in 1920s San Francisco. The narrative explores themes of greed, betrayal, and moral ambiguity as Spade navigates a treacherous landscape filled with deceit and murder. Hammett's concise prose and sharp dialogue reflect the disillusionment of the era and have significantly influenced the detective fiction genre. Tone and style: gritty, economical, sharp dialogue. Pacing: fast-paced, plot-driven. Themes: greed, betrayal, moral ambiguity. Setting: 1920s San Francisco. About the author: Samuel Dashiell Hammett was an American writer of hard-boiled detective novels and short stories. He was also a screenwriter and political activist. Among the characters he created are Sam Spade, Nick and Nora Charles, The Continental Op and the comic strip character Secret Agent X-9.

title: I Deliver Parcels in Beijing
author: Hu Anyan
text: Published 2025. Genre: Biography & Memoir. I Deliver Parcels in Beijing is a first-person account of Hu Anyan's experiences in the gig economy, detailing his various short-term jobs in megacities during the COVID lockdowns. The narrative highlights the pressures faced by young workers today, exploring themes of brutal working conditions and the search for meaning through reading and writing. With a blend of humor and honesty, Hu reflects on his struggles and the dehumanizing aspects of contemporary work life. Tone and style: honest, humorous, reflective. Pacing: measured, anecdotal. Themes: gig economy, work struggles, self-discovery. Setting: contemporary China, during COVID-19.

title: I Have Some Questions For You
author: Rebecca Makkai
text: Published 2023. Genre: Literary Fiction. The novel follows Bodie Kane, a film professor and podcaster who returns to her former boarding school to teach. As she revisits the past, particularly the murder of her roommate Thalia Keith, Bodie grapples with the flawed investigation that led to the conviction of the school's athletic trainer. This leads her to question her memories and the true nature of the events surrounding Thalia's death. Tone and style: thoughtful, immersive, engaging. Pacing: slow-burn, character-driven. Themes: memory, trauma, justice, investigation. Setting: 1990s New Hampshire boarding school. About the author: Rebecca Makkai is an American novelist and short story writer. She is best known for writing The Great Believers (2018) and I Have Some Questions for You (2023), which have been positively received by critics and won awards such as the Los Angeles Times Book Prize for Fiction, the Andrew Carnegie Medal for Excellence in Fiction, and the Libby Book Award.

title: The Snakehead
author: Patrick Radden Keefe
text: Published 2009. Genre: True Crime. The Snakehead explores the life of Sister Ping, a grandmother who ran a vast human smuggling operation from her noodle shop in New York's Chinatown. The book details the FBI's investigation into her activities and examines the broader issues surrounding immigration, including the challenges faced by desperate immigrants and the underground economy that exploits them. It weaves a narrative that combines elements of crime, corruption, and the complexities of the American immigration system. Tone and style: engaging, investigative, narrative-driven. Pacing: fast-paced, investigative. Themes: immigration, crime, exploitation, corruption. Setting: New York's Chinatown and the US immigration system. About the author: Patrick Radden Keefe is an American writer and investigative journalist. He is the author of six books—Chatter (2005), The Snakehead (2009), Say Nothing (2018), Empire of Pain (2021), Rogues (2022), and London Falling (2026)—and has written extensively for many publications, including The New Yorker, Slate, and The New York Times Magazine. He is a staff writer at The New Yorker.

title: The Wager
author: David Grann
text: Published 2025. Genre: True Crime. The Wager recounts the harrowing tale of a British shipwreck in 1740 during an imperial conflict with Spain. After the HMS Wager wrecks off the coast of Patagonia, the surviving crew members face starvation and internal conflict, leading to accusations of mutiny and murder. The narrative culminates in a court martial that explores themes of survival, authority, and the darker aspects of human nature. Tone and style: gripping, detailed, narrative-driven. Pacing: fast-paced, suspenseful. Themes: survival, mutiny, imperialism, human behavior. Setting: 18th-century maritime conflict, South America. About the author: David Elliot Grann is an American journalist, a staff writer for The New Yorker, and author.

title: The Devotion of Suspect X
author: Keigo Higashino
text: Published 2011. Genre: Mystery. The Devotion of Suspect X follows Yasuko Hanaoka, a single mother who kills her abusive ex-husband in self-defense. Her neighbor, Ishigami, a mathematics teacher, helps her cover up the crime, leading to a complex investigation by Detective Kusanagi and his friend, physicist Yukawa. The story unfolds as a battle of wits between Ishigami and Yukawa, who seeks to uncover the truth behind the murder. Tone and style: intelligent, suspenseful, intricate. Pacing: methodical, tension-building. Themes: sacrifice, intellect, morality. Setting: contemporary Japan. About the author: Keigo Higashino  was a Japanese author chiefly known for his mystery novels. He served as the 13th President of Mystery Writers of Japan from 2009 to 2013. Higashino won major Japanese awards for his books, almost twenty of which have been turned into films and television series.

title: The Wizard of Earthsea
author: Ursula K LeGuin
text: Published 2003. Genre: Fantasy. The Wizard of Earthsea follows Ged, a young boy with innate magical abilities, who becomes an apprentice to a powerful wizard. As he grows into adulthood, Ged must confront the dark forces he inadvertently unleashed upon the world, learning about the balance of power and the importance of self-acceptance. This coming-of-age story explores themes of identity and the consequences of one's actions. Tone and style: lyrical, introspective, rich imagery. Pacing: moderate, character-driven. Themes: identity, power, self-discovery. Setting: the archipelago of Earthsea, a fantasy world. About the author: Ursula Kroeber Le Guin was an American author. She is best known for her works of speculative fiction, including science fiction works set in her Hainish universe, and the Earthsea fantasy series. Her work was first published in 1959, and her literary career spanned nearly sixty years, producing more than twenty novels and more than a hundred short stories, in addition to poetry, literary criticism, translations, and children's books. Frequently described as an author of science fiction, Le Guin has also been called a "major voice in American Letters". Le Guin said that she would prefer to be known as an "American novelist".

title: The Anarchy
author: William Dalrymple
text: Published 2019. Genre: History. The Anarchy explores the rise of the East India Company and its transformation from a trading entity into a colonial power in India. It details the company's defeat of the Mughal emperor in 1765 and the establishment of a new administration that exploited local resources and governance. Dalrymple presents a historical narrative that highlights the implications of corporate power and colonialism. Tone and style: engaging, analytical, narrative-driven. Pacing: detailed, chronological. Themes: colonialism, corporate power, imperialism. Setting: 18th-century India and the British Empire. About the author: William Benedict Hamilton-Dalrymple is a Scottish historian, art historian, indologist, curator, broadcaster, critic and author.

title: Three Bags Full
author: Leonie Swann
text: Published 2010-10-29. Genre: Mystery. In a quaint Irish village, a flock of sheep investigates the murder of their beloved shepherd, George, who is found dead with a spade. Led by the clever Miss Maple, the sheep engage in philosophical discussions and reconnaissance missions to uncover the killer among the villagers, all while grappling with their own emotions and relationships. This unique murder mystery combines humor and introspection through the eyes of its ovine detectives. Tone and style: witty, philosophical, charming. Pacing: light-hearted, character-driven. Themes: friendship, loyalty, existential inquiry. Setting: rural Ireland, cozy village atmosphere. About the author: Leonie Swann is a pseudonymous German crime writer.

title: Hawaii's Story by Hawaii's Queen
author: Queen Liliuokalani
text: Published 1898. Genre: Biography & Memoir. In "Hawaii's Story by Hawaii's Queen," Queen Liliuokalani recounts her life as the last monarch of Hawaii, detailing her upbringing, reign, and the events leading to the overthrow of the Hawaiian Kingdom. Written during her imprisonment, the book serves as both a personal memoir and a historical account of the political turmoil in Hawaii in the late 19th century. Liliuokalani's narrative emphasizes her commitment to her people and the cultural significance of her reign. Tone and style: personal, reflective, historical. Pacing: measured, narrative-driven. Themes: monarchy, colonialism, identity. Setting: Hawaii in the late 19th century. About the author: Liliʻuokalani was the only queen regnant and the last sovereign monarch of the Hawaiian Kingdom, ruling from January 29, 1891, until the overthrow of the Hawaiian Kingdom on January 17, 1893, in a coup that was led by the Committee of Safety, composed of seven foreign residents and six Hawaiian Kingdom subjects of American descent in Honolulu. The composer of "Aloha ʻOe" and numerous other works, she wrote her autobiography Hawaiʻi's Story by Hawaiʻi's Queen (1898) during her imprisonment following the overthrow.

title: Shanghai Girls
author: Lisa See
text: Published 2009. Genre: Historical Fiction. "Shanghai Girls" follows the lives of two sisters, Pearl and May, who flee Shanghai in the late 1930s and navigate their new lives in Los Angeles amidst the challenges of war and cultural displacement. The novel explores themes of family loyalty, identity, and the immigrant experience as they confront prejudice and strive to build a future in America. Tone and style: emotional, vivid, detailed. Pacing: measured, character-driven. Themes: sisterhood, immigration, identity, resilience. Setting: 1930s Shanghai and Los Angeles. About the author: Lisa See is an American writer and novelist.

title: Ultimate Obsession
author: David Gessner
text: Genre: Biography & Memoir. Ultimate Obsession explores the author's deep engagement with nature and the environment, reflecting on personal experiences and broader ecological themes. It delves into the complexities of human relationships with the natural world, emphasizing the importance of conservation and awareness. Tone and style: reflective, personal, lyrical. Pacing: measured, contemplative. Themes: nature, obsession, conservation. Setting: contemporary environmental landscape. About the author: David Gessner is an American essayist, memoirist, nature writer, editor, and cartoonist.

title: His Majesty's Dragon: Book One of Temeraire
author: Naomi Novik
text: Genre: Fantasy. Set during the Napoleonic Wars, this novel follows Captain Will Laurence, who discovers a dragon egg aboard a captured French ship. When the egg hatches, Laurence bonds with the dragon, named Temeraire, and they embark on a journey that intertwines military strategy with the challenges of navigating a world where dragons are used in warfare. Together, they face the complexities of loyalty, friendship, and the impact of war on both humans and dragons. Tone and style: adventurous, detailed, historical. Pacing: steady, character-driven. Themes: friendship, loyalty, war, alternate history. Setting: Napoleonic Wars, Europe. About the author: Naomi Novik is an American author of speculative fiction. She is known for her Temeraire series (2006–2016), an alternate history of the Napoleonic Wars involving dragons; and her Scholomance trilogy (2020–2022). Her standalone fantasy novels Uprooted (2015) and Spinning Silver (2018) were inspired by Polish folklore and the Rumpelstiltskin fairy tale respectively. She also helped create the Organization for Transformative Works and was a cofounder of their project Archive of Our Own. Novik has won many awards for her work, including the Alex, Audie, British Fantasy, Locus, Mythopoeic and Nebula Awards.

title: Either/Or
author: Elif Batuman
text: Published 2022. Genre: Literary Fiction. In "Either/Or," Selin returns to Harvard for her sophomore year, reflecting on her experiences and relationships, particularly her thoughts about Ivan. The novel explores themes of love, identity, and the complexities of young adulthood as Selin navigates her academic and personal life. Tone and style: introspective, conversational, witty. Pacing: measured, character-driven. Themes: love, identity, coming of age. Setting: Harvard University in the 1990s. About the author: Elif Batuman is an American author, academic, and journalist. She is the author of three books: a memoir, The Possessed (2010), the novel The Idiot (2017), which was a finalist for the 2018 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction, and Either/Or (2022). Batuman is a staff writer for The New Yorker.

title: The Quants
author: Scott Patterson
text: Published 2000. Genre: Business & Economics. The Quants explores the rise of quantitative analysts in the financial world, focusing on figures like Peter Muller, Ken Griffin, Cliff Asness, and Boaz Weinstein. It details their innovative approaches to trading using complex mathematical formulas and high-speed computers, which ultimately led to significant financial gains and losses. The narrative also reflects on the implications of their methods and the potential risks they introduced to the financial market. Tone and style: engaging, analytical, cautionary. Pacing: fast-paced, narrative-driven. Themes: ambition, risk, financial markets, technology. Setting: 21st-century Wall Street and financial institutions. About the author: Scott Patterson is an American actor and former baseball player. He is known for his roles as Luke Danes in Gilmore Girls (2000–2007) and Peter Strahm in the Saw film series (2007–2009). He also starred as Michael Buchanan in the NBC drama series The Event and as a Tenctonese alien commander in the TV film Alien Nation: Dark Horizon. Since 2023, Patterson has played the recurring role of Harry 'Sully' Sullivan on the Canadian television series Sullivan's Crossing.

title: This Side of Paradise
author: F.Scott (Francis Scott) Fitzgerald
text: Genre: Literary Fiction. This Side of Paradise follows the life of Amory Blaine, a young man navigating love, ambition, and the complexities of society in the early 20th century. The novel explores themes of self-discovery and the impact of wealth and privilege on personal relationships. Through Amory's experiences, Fitzgerald critiques the American Dream and the disillusionment that often accompanies it. Tone and style: lyrical, introspective, modernist. Pacing: measured, character-driven. Themes: identity, love, disillusionment, social class. Setting: early 20th-century America.

title: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People
author: Stephen R. Covey
text: Published 1989. Genre: Self-Help & Personal Development. The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People outlines a principle-centered approach to personal and professional effectiveness. Covey presents seven habits that can help individuals achieve their goals and improve their relationships by focusing on character and ethical behavior. The book emphasizes proactive behavior, prioritization, and effective communication as essential components of success. Tone and style: pragmatic, motivational, clear. Pacing: structured, methodical. Themes: personal development, effectiveness, leadership. Setting: contemporary self-help context. About the author: Stephen Richards Covey was an American educator, author, businessman, and speaker. His most popular book is The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People. His other books include First Things First, Principle-Centered Leadership, The 7 Habits of Highly Effective Families, The 8th Habit, and The Leader In Me: How Schools and Parents Around the World Are Inspiring Greatness, One Child at a Time. In 1996, Time magazine named him one of the 25 most influential people. He was a professor at the Jon M. Huntsman School of Business at Utah State University (USU) at the time of his death.

title: The Big Short: Inside the Doomsday Machine
author: Michael Lewis
text: Genre: Business & Economics. The Big Short explores the causes and consequences of the 2008 financial crisis, focusing on the individuals who predicted the collapse of the housing market and profited from it. Through a mix of personal stories and detailed analysis, it highlights the complexities of the financial instruments that contributed to the crisis. The book sheds light on the systemic failures within financial institutions and regulatory bodies that allowed the crisis to occur. Tone and style: insightful, engaging, journalistic. Pacing: fast-paced, narrative-driven. Themes: financial crisis, risk, greed, systemic failure. Setting: 2000s American financial landscape. About the author: Michael Monroe Lewis is an American author and financial journalist. He has also been a contributing editor to Vanity Fair since 2009, writing mostly on business, finance, and economics. He is known for his nonfiction work, particularly his coverage of financial crises and behavioral finance.

title: A Random Walk Down Wall Street
author: Burton G. Malkiel
text: Published 1973. Genre: Business & Economics. This book provides an overview of investment strategies and market behavior, emphasizing the importance of a diversified portfolio. It discusses the concept of the 'random walk' theory, suggesting that stock prices are unpredictable and that a long-term investment strategy is more effective than trying to time the market. Malkiel also offers practical advice for investors of all ages on how to manage their portfolios. Tone and style: informative, accessible, pragmatic. Pacing: measured, methodical. Themes: investment strategies, market behavior, portfolio management. Setting: contemporary financial markets. About the author: Burton Gordon Malkiel is an American economist, financial executive, and writer most noted for his classic finance book A Random Walk Down Wall Street.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
text: Published 2015. Genre: Literary Fiction. The Brothers Karamazov is a philosophical novel that explores the moral struggles of three brothers—Dmitri, Ivan, and Alexei Karamazov—against the backdrop of their father's murder. It delves into themes of faith, doubt, free will, and the nature of evil, reflecting the complex social and spiritual issues of 19th-century Russia. The interactions between the brothers and their father highlight deep existential questions and the search for meaning in a chaotic world. Tone and style: philosophical, introspective, dense. Pacing: slow-burn, character-driven. Themes: faith, morality, family, free will, existentialism. Setting: 19th-century Russia. About the author: Fyodor Mikhailovich Dostoevsky was a Russian philosopher, novelist, short-story writer, essayist and journalist. He is regarded as one of the greatest novelists in both Russian and world literature, and many of his works are considered highly influential masterpieces. Dostoevsky's literary works explore the human condition in the troubled political, social and spiritual atmospheres of 19th-century Russia, and engage with a variety of philosophical and religious themes. His most acclaimed novels include Crime and Punishment (1866), The Idiot (1869), Demons (1872), The Adolescent (1875) and The Brothers Karamazov (1880). His Notes from Underground, a novella published in 1864, is considered one of the first works of existentialist literature.

title: Where Good Ideas Come From
author: Steven Johnson
text: Published 2010. Genre: Business & Economics. This book explores the history of innovation, focusing on the concept of the 'slow hunch'—the idea that new ideas often emerge from the gradual accumulation of older concepts. Johnson introduces the term 'adjacent possible' to describe how innovations evolve by building on existing ideas, highlighting the shift from individual invention to collaborative efforts for the public good. Tone and style: insightful, engaging, analytical. Pacing: measured, exploratory. Themes: innovation, collaboration, idea generation. Setting: historical context of innovation and creativity. About the author: Steven Johnson may refer to:

title: Anathem
author: Neal Stephenson
text: Published 2008. Genre: Science Fiction. Anathem follows Fraa Erasmas, a young avout living in a secluded community dedicated to mathematics and philosophy, as he prepares for a rare event called Apert. This celebration allows the avout to venture into the outside world, which has been marked by historical violence against their community. As Erasmas reconnects with his past, he faces unforeseen challenges that threaten both his cloistered life and the broader world, leading him to play a crucial role in averting global disaster. Tone and style: intellectual, intricate, imaginative. Pacing: slow-burn, philosophical exploration. Themes: knowledge, society, conflict, adaptation. Setting: alternate world with a focus on mathematics and philosophy. About the author: Neal Town Stephenson is an American writer known for his works of speculative fiction. His novels have been categorized as science fiction, historical fiction, cyberpunk, and baroque.

title: The Prince
author: Niccolo Machiavelli
text: Published 1515. Genre: Politics & Current Affairs. The Prince is a political treatise by Niccolò Machiavelli that serves as a guide for new rulers on how to maintain power and achieve glory. It discusses the use of pragmatic and sometimes immoral tactics in politics, arguing that the ends can justify the means. Written in the vernacular Italian, it marked a shift in political writing during the Renaissance. Tone and style: cynical, direct, analytical. Pacing: concise, argument-driven. Themes: power, morality, political strategy. Setting: 16th-century Italy. About the author: Niccolò di Bernardo dei Machiavelli was a Florentine diplomat, author, philosopher, and historian who lived during the Italian Renaissance. He is best known for his political treatise The Prince, written around 1513 but not published until 1532, five years after his death. He has often been called the father of modern political philosophy and political science.

title: High Fidelity
author: Nick Hornby
text: Published 1995. Genre: Literary Fiction. Rob, the owner of a small record shop, struggles with his relationships and commitment issues. After his girlfriend decides to leave him, he reflects on his past relationships and his obsession with music as he navigates his feelings. The novel explores themes of love, loss, and the complexities of modern relationships. Tone and style: wry, conversational, introspective. Pacing: character-driven, reflective. Themes: relationships, music, self-discovery. Setting: contemporary London. About the author: Nicholas Peter John Hornby is an English writer. He is best known for his memoir Fever Pitch (1992) and novels High Fidelity (1995) and About a Boy (1998), all of which were adapted into feature films. Hornby's work frequently touches upon music, sport, and the aimless and obsessive natures of his protagonists. His books have sold more than 5 million copies worldwide as of 2018. In a 2004 poll for the BBC, Hornby was named the 29th most influential person in British culture. He has received two Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay nominations for An Education (2009), and Brooklyn (2015).

title: Drive: The Surprising Truth About What Motivates Us
author: Daniel H. Pink
text: Genre: Business & Economics. This book explores the psychology of motivation, arguing that traditional rewards and punishments are not as effective as previously thought. Pink presents a new framework for understanding what drives human behavior, emphasizing intrinsic motivation and the importance of autonomy, mastery, and purpose in achieving high performance and satisfaction. Tone and style: insightful, engaging, accessible. Pacing: structured, argument-driven. Themes: motivation, psychology, human behavior. Setting: contemporary workplace and personal development. About the author: Daniel H. Pink is an American non-fiction writer who has authored seven New York Times bestsellers. He was host and a co-executive producer of the National Geographic Channel social science TV series Crowd Control. From 1995 to 1997, he was the chief speechwriter for Vice President Al Gore.

title: A Supposedly Fun Thing I'll Never Do Again
author: David Foster Wallace
text: Published 1997. Genre: Literary Fiction. This collection of essays and stories by David Foster Wallace examines various aspects of contemporary life, including mental health, relationships, and the absurdities of modern culture. Notable pieces include 'The Depressed Person', which delves into a woman's struggles with depression, and 'Brief Interviews with Hideous Men', a series of darkly humorous vignettes about men's fears and insecurities. Wallace's unique voice and insightful observations highlight the complexities of human experience. Tone and style: witty, introspective, experimental. Pacing: varied, reflective. Themes: mental health, relationships, modern absurdity. Setting: contemporary America. About the author: David Foster Wallace was an American writer and professor who published novels, short stories, and essays. He is most widely known for his 1996 novel Infinite Jest. In 2008, David Ulin wrote for the Los Angeles Times that Wallace was "one of the most influential and innovative writers of the last twenty years".

title: Made to Stick: Why Some Ideas Survive and Others Die
author: Chip Heath, Dan Heath
text: Genre: Business & Economics. This book explores why certain ideas are more memorable and impactful than others. The authors present a framework for creating sticky ideas, focusing on principles such as simplicity, unexpectedness, concreteness, credibility, emotions, and stories. Through various examples, they illustrate how to apply these principles in communication and marketing. Tone and style: engaging, practical, insightful. Pacing: structured, example-driven. Themes: communication, marketing, idea retention. Setting: contemporary business and communication contexts.

title: Bloomberg by Bloomberg
author: Michael R. Bloomberg
text: Published 2018. Genre: Biography & Memoir. In this book, Michael R. Bloomberg shares his insights and experiences from his career as a businessman and politician. He discusses the principles that guided him in building Bloomberg L.P. and his tenure as mayor of New York City, offering a perspective on leadership, innovation, and public service. Tone and style: insightful, straightforward, reflective. Pacing: measured, anecdotal. Themes: leadership, innovation, public service. Setting: business and political landscape of New York City. About the author: Michael Rubens Bloomberg is an American businessman and politician. He is the majority owner and co-founder of Bloomberg L.P., and was its CEO from 1981 to 2001, and again from 2014 to 2023. He served as the 109th mayor of New York City from 2002 to 2013. He was a lifelong Democrat until 2001, when he switched to the Republican Party to run for mayor, and later becoming an Independent in 2007. Bloomberg is the most recent mayor of New York City to serve as a Republican or Independent. In 2018, he rejoined the Democratic Party, after which he ran an unsuccessful campaign for the 2020 Democratic nomination for president of the United States. Bloomberg is a centibillionaire, worth $109.4 billion as of March 2026, making him the 18th richest person in the world.

title: Culture and Anarchy
author: Matthew Arnold
text: Published 1869. Genre: Social Science. In "Culture and Anarchy," Matthew Arnold explores the relationship between culture and society, questioning the essence and necessity of culture in the face of societal unrest in mid-Victorian England. He contrasts the ideal of culture, which he views as the pursuit of perfection, with the chaos of anarchy, advocating for the importance of cultural development as a means to address social issues. The essays reflect on the historical context of Arnold's time and continue to resonate with contemporary discussions on multiculturalism and post-modernism. Tone and style: analytical, critical, reflective. Pacing: methodical, essayistic. Themes: culture, society, perfection, anarchy. Setting: mid-Victorian England. About the author: Matthew Arnold was an English poet and cultural critic. He was the son of Thomas Arnold, the headmaster of Rugby School, and brother of both Tom Arnold, literary professor, and William Delafield Arnold, novelist and colonial administrator. He has been characterised as a sage writer, a type of writer who chastises and instructs the reader on contemporary social issues. He was also an inspector of schools for thirty-five years, and supported the concept of state-regulated secondary education.

title: Hyperion
author: Dan Simmons
text: Published 1989. Genre: Science Fiction. In the 29th century, the Hegemony of Man is a vast interstellar civilization facing threats from the Ousters and the TechnoCore, a group of AIs. The story revolves around a pilgrimage to the Time Tombs on the planet Hyperion, where each pilgrim shares their personal tale of how they were chosen for this journey, set against the backdrop of impending invasion and the mysterious Shrike creature. Tone and style: epic, intricate, philosophical. Pacing: character-driven, interwoven narratives. Themes: faith, sacrifice, the nature of time. Setting: 29th-century interstellar civilization. About the author: Daniel Joseph Simmons was an American science fiction and horror writer. He was the author of the Hyperion Cantos and the Ilium/Olympos cycles, among other works that span the science fiction, horror, and fantasy genres, sometimes within a single novel. Simmons's genre-intermingling Song of Kali (1985) won the World Fantasy Award. He also wrote mysteries and thrillers, some of which feature the continuing character Joe Kurtz.

title: The Information: A History, a Theory, a Flood
author: James Gleick
text: Genre: History. This book explores the concept of information, tracing its history from early communication methods to the digital age. Gleick examines how information has shaped human culture, science, and technology, presenting it as a fundamental element of modern life. The narrative weaves together historical anecdotes and theoretical insights, illustrating the transformative power of information. Tone and style: insightful, narrative nonfiction. Pacing: measured, exploratory. Themes: information theory, communication, technology. Setting: historical and contemporary contexts of information. About the author: James Gleick is an American author and historian of science whose work has chronicled the cultural impact of modern technology. Recognized for his writing about complex subjects through the techniques of narrative nonfiction, he has been called "one of the great science writers of all time". He is part of the inspiration for Jurassic Park character Ian Malcolm.

title: Savages
author: Don Winslow
text: Published 2010. Genre: Thriller. Savages follows two marijuana growers, Ben and Chon, who live a peaceful life in California until their girlfriend, Ophelia, is kidnapped by a Mexican drug cartel. The story explores their desperate attempts to rescue her, leading to a violent confrontation with the cartel and a moral reckoning about their choices. The novel delves into themes of loyalty, love, and the consequences of the drug trade. Tone and style: gritty, fast-paced, contemporary. Pacing: fast-paced, action-driven. Themes: loyalty, love, drug trade, violence. Setting: modern California and Mexico. About the author: Don Winslow is an American author best known for his crime novels including Savages, The Force and the Cartel Trilogy.

title: The Hunger Games
author: Suzanne Collins
text: Published 2008. Genre: Young Adult Fiction. The Hunger Games follows 16-year-old Katniss Everdeen in the dystopian nation of Panem, where the Capitol exerts control over the districts. Each year, the Capitol hosts the Hunger Games, a brutal televised competition where one boy and one girl from each district fight to the death. Katniss volunteers to take her sister's place in the Games, leading her to navigate complex themes of survival, sacrifice, and rebellion. Tone and style: gritty, fast-paced, first-person. Pacing: intense, action-driven. Themes: survival, oppression, rebellion, sacrifice. Setting: dystopian future, post-apocalyptic North America. About the author: Suzanne Collins is an American author and television writer who is best known as the author of the young adult dystopian fiction book series The Hunger Games. She is also the author of the children's fantasy series The Underland Chronicles.

title: The Great Stagnation
author: Tyler Cowen
text: Published 2011. Genre: Business & Economics. In 'The Great Stagnation', Tyler Cowen analyzes the reasons behind America's economic stagnation, highlighting the decline of easy economic gains since the 1970s. He argues that the country has reached a technological plateau, leading to flat median wages and rising unemployment. Cowen critiques both political parties for their ineffective solutions and calls for a renewed focus on innovation and scientific enterprise to revitalize the economy. Tone and style: analytical, engaging, critical. Pacing: methodical, argument-driven. Themes: economic stagnation, innovation, political critique. Setting: contemporary American economy. About the author: Tyler Cowen is an American economist, author, and public intellectual. He is the Holbert L. Harris Professor of Economics at George Mason University and serves as chairman of the university’s Mercatus Center. Cowen is widely known for his blog Marginal Revolution, which he has co-authored with Alex Tabarrok since 2003, and for hosting the interview podcast Conversations with Tyler.

title: The New New Thing: A Silicon Valley Story
author: Michael Lewis
text: Genre: Biography & Memoir. The New New Thing follows Jim Clark, a Silicon Valley entrepreneur, as he navigates the tech boom of the late 1990s. The book explores themes of innovation, ambition, and the rapid evolution of the internet economy, highlighting Clark's ventures such as Netscape. It provides insights into the culture of Silicon Valley and the personalities that drive its success. Tone and style: insightful, engaging, journalistic. Pacing: fast-paced, anecdotal. Themes: innovation, entrepreneurship, technology. Setting: Silicon Valley during the tech boom of the late 1990s. About the author: Michael Monroe Lewis is an American author and financial journalist. He has also been a contributing editor to Vanity Fair since 2009, writing mostly on business, finance, and economics. He is known for his nonfiction work, particularly his coverage of financial crises and behavioral finance.

title: Mockingjay
author: Suzanne Collins
text: Published 2010. Genre: Young Adult Fiction. In "Mockingjay," Katniss Everdeen becomes the symbol of rebellion against the oppressive Capitol as the war escalates. Struggling with her role as the Mockingjay, she faces personal and political challenges while navigating the complexities of leadership and sacrifice. The story explores themes of loyalty, propaganda, and the consequences of war. Tone and style: intense, dramatic, engaging. Pacing: fast-paced, action-driven. Themes: rebellion, sacrifice, identity. Setting: dystopian future, war-torn Panem. About the author: Suzanne Collins is an American author and television writer who is best known as the author of the young adult dystopian fiction book series The Hunger Games. She is also the author of the children's fantasy series The Underland Chronicles.

title: WAR
author: Sebastian Junger
text: Published 2010. Genre: Biography & Memoir. In 'WAR', Sebastian Junger explores the experiences of soldiers in combat, focusing on the psychological impacts of war. Drawing from his time embedded with a U.S. Army unit in Afghanistan, he examines themes of brotherhood, fear, and the challenges of reintegration into civilian life. The book provides a raw and unfiltered look at the realities of modern warfare. Tone and style: intense, reflective, journalistic. Pacing: immersive, anecdotal. Themes: combat, brotherhood, psychological impact of war. Setting: Afghanistan during the War on Terror. About the author: Sebastian Junger is an American journalist, author and filmmaker.
